questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Fertilization in human takes place in the womb.
Zygote contains haploid number of chromosomes.
Primary oocyte inhibits the process of oogenesis.
questions.solution:
After the sperm’s receptors come into contact with the egg’s jelly layer and the acrosomal enzymes are released and break down the jelly layer, the sperm head comes in contact with the plasma membrane of the egg. When the two plasma membranes contact one another, signals in the egg are initiated.

First, Na+ channels in the egg open, allowing Na+ to flood into the egg. This causes a depolarization of the egg from its normal resting potential of -70 mV.

While depolarization is occurring, the remainder of the jelly layer is dissolving. With the dissolution of the jelly layer and the depolarization of the plasma membrane, the first block to preventing fertilization by multiple sperm is put into place.

Within 1/10th of a second of contact, the fast block to polyspermy is initiated. The cortical granules release its secretion causing the change in the composition of the zona pellucida membrane.

Slow block:

The cortical vesicles contain enzymes that cause a number of changes to occur in the egg.

1.  The egg’s sperm receptors are removed.

2.  H2O is absorbed, causing the membrane to swell and push the vitelline membrane away from the plasma membrane.

3.  The vitelline membrane hardens.

questions.solution: Oogenesis starts with the division of oogonia (gamete mother cells) giving rise to primary oocyte which enters into prophase - I of the meiotic division and gets temporarily arrested at this stage. These primary oocyte gets surrounded by primary, secondary, and tertiary follicles respectively. The tertiary follicle grows in size and completes its first meiotic division to give rise to the haploid secondary oocyte. This secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called zona pellucida surrounding it. During fertilization, the sperm enters into the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane. This induces the completion of the meiotic division (2<sup>nd</sup> division) of the secondary oocyte. The second meiotic division is also unequal and results in the formation of a second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid).

questions.solution: Mammary glands are modified sweat glands and characteristics of mammalian females. In human males it is a vestigial organ. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Parturition is induced by
questions.solution: Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism which is triggered by the fully formed foetus and the placenta called foetal ejection complex. This encompasses the mild uterine contractions in response to the trigger. A developing foetus secretes hormones from its adrenal glands. These hormones diffuse into the maternal blood and accumulate to stimulate the release of oxytocin (birth hormone) from the mother’s posterior pituitary. Oxytocin acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger contractions, which in turn stimulates the further secretion. The stimulatory reflex between the uterine contraction and oxytocin secretion continues resulting in stronger and stronger contractions leading to the expulsion of the baby out of the uterus through the birth canal.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct description of follicular phase of menstrual cycle?
options: Primary follicles in the ovary grow to become a fully mature Graafian follicle and simultaneously the endometrium of uterus regenerates through proliferation.
The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone which is essential for maintenance of the endometrium.
Both LH and FSH attain a peak level about 10<sup>th</sup> day leading to rupture of Graafian follicle.

questions.solution:
Phases of the menstrual cycle:

I. Menstrual phase (3–5 days): Breakdown of the endometrial lining of the uterus and its blood vessels occurs that comes out of the vagina as menstrual fluid.

II. Follicular phase: Primary follicles grow to become Graafian follicles. Regeneration of lost endometrium starts with hormonal changes, and a gradual increase in the release of gonadotropins like LH and FSH takes place, which stimulates the follicular development and estrogen release by the growing follicles.

III. Ovulatory phase (14th day): LH surge occurs with a peak concentration of LH during the mid-cycle, that ruptures the Graafian follicle and releases an ovum (ovulation).

IV. Luteal phase (next 14 days): The remnants of the Graafian follicle are transformed into the corpus luteum that secretes large amounts of progesterone to maintain the endometrium (necessary for implantation of the fertilized ovum).

questions.solution: The process of fusion of a sperm with an ovum is called fertilization. During fertilization, a sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida layer of the ovum and induces changes in the membrane that block the entry of additional sperms. Thus, it ensures that only one sperm can fertilize an ovum. The secretions of the acrosome help the sperm enter into the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane. In contact with the surface of egg covering, the acrosome releases hydrolytic enzymes (also called sperm lysins) present in it. This is known as acrosomal reaction. Acrosome reaction results in dissolving of corona cells and degeneration of zona pellucida which helps in sperm penetration.

The back and forth movement of the tail makes the sperm to move. ATP produced by mitochondria supplies the energy for this process.

questions.solution: It consists of a population of Sertoli cells and a spermatogenic cell line. Sertoli cells span the thickness of the seminiferous epithelium. Sertoli cell characteristics including the distribution of their intercellular junctions, divide the seminiferous epithelium into a basal compartment containing only spermatogonia and an adluminal compartment containing primary and secondary spermatocytes, spermatids, and spermatozoa. The differentiation of spermatogonia into spermatids does not begin until puberty. Thus, the seminiferous epithelium does not contain spermatids prior to puberty like all epithelial layers, the basal surface of the seminiferous epithelium is bounded by the basement membrane.

B. Mons pubis is a cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair.
C. A primary spermatocyte completes the second meiotic division leading to the formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes, which have only 23 chromosomes each.
D. The secondary follicles get surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca; they are called tertiary follicles.
questions.solution:
Statements C and D are incorrect.

C. Some spermatogonia (termed as primary spermatocytes) periodically undergo meiosis. A primary spermatocyte completes meiosis-I (reduction division) and gives rise to 2 equal-sized cells called secondary spermatocytes (n = 23). Both secondary spermatocytes undergo meiosis-II (equational division) to produce 2 equal spermatids (n) each.

D. Primary follicles are converted to secondary follicles by getting surrounded by a few more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca. Following changes occur in the secondary follicle after which it is immediately converted to tertiary follicle:

I. Development of a fluid-filled cavity called antrum.

II. Differentiation of Theca layer into theca interna (inner) and theca externa (outer).

III. Primary oocyte grows in size, completes meiosis-I (unequal division) resulting in the formation of a large haploid secondary oocyte and a small first polar body. Tertiary follicle changes into the mature follicle (Graafian follicle).

Meiosis-II leads to the formation of spermatids
Production of one sperm and 3 polar bodies

questions.solution:
Steps involved in Spermatogenesis
 
Step 1 Spermatogonia (2n = 46) are present in the inside wall of seminiferous tubules. Spermatogonium divides mitotically to increase in number.
Step 2 Some spermatogonia (termed as primary spermatocytes) periodically undergo meiosis. A primary spermatocyte completes meiosis-I (reduction division) and gives rise to 2 equal-sized cells called secondary spermatocytes (n = 23).
Step 3 Both secondary spermatocytes undergo meiosis –II (equational division) to produce 2 equal spermatids (n) each.
Step 4 Each spermatid is transformed into spermatozoa (sperms) by the process of spermiogenesis.
Step 5 After spermiogenesis, the head of sperms becomes embedded in the sertoli cells. Sperms are finally released from the seminiferous tubules by the process called spermiation.

D. Capacitation           4. Mammary gland
E  Colostrum               5. Sperm activation
questions.solution:
Hyaluronidase or sperm lysin is an enzyme released by acrosome of the sperm by breaking down of the membrane surrounding it.
Corpus luteum is a yellowish mass of tissue that forms from the granulosa cells in the cavity of a Graafian follicle in the ovary of a mammal after the release of the egg cell. It secretes the hormone progesterone.
Gastrulation is the phase of embryonic development during which the cells of blastula move in small masses or as a sheet of cells to attain the final locations. such movement is called morphogenetic movement.
Sperms in the female genital tract are made capable of fertilizing the egg by secretions of the female genital tract. These secretions of the female tract remove coating substances deposited on the surface of the sperms particularly those on the acrosome. It exposes the receptor sites on acrosome and leads to sperms activations. This phenomenon is called capacitation.
Colostrum is a liquid with high nitrogen content, antibodies and vitamins that is secreted from the mammary glands before and just after giving birth.

A woman conceives as well as becomes pregnant about a week after fertilization

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following blocks the entry of additional sperm, once a single sperm cell encounters ova?
questions.solution: The zona pellucida (ZP) is an important, integral structure for the egg both before and after fertilization. The zona pellucida (ZP) is a name given to a clear (lucid) zone or region that surrounds the unfertilized egg and works to keep out the additional sperm that hangs around after the first union. It even stays close to the developing cells after fertilization to help out along the road to implantation in the uterus or womb.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following secretes the hormone responsible for relaxing pubic symphysis during the childbirth?
questions.solution: Relaxin is secreted into the circulation by the corpus luteum in the ovary. During pregnancy it is also released from the placenta. There is also some evidence that relaxin can relax the ligaments at the front of the pelvis to ease delivery of the baby.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following structures is responsible for the release of sperm in the lumen of seminiferous tubules?
questions.solution: The supporting cells (Sertoli cells) are located within the seminiferous tubules. Their task is the creation of a blood-testicular barrier. Sertoli cells sit on a basal membrane.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Arrange the formation of the following cells in the ovary in the sequential order:

i) Ovum
ii) Primary follicle
iii) Primary oocytes
iv) Graafian follicle
questions.solution:
In an ovary, there are millions of oocytes. An oocyte is not the same thing as a germ cell. The germ cells develop in the fetal ovary and before birth begin meiosis, and then freeze right at the start of the first meiotic division. These cells are stopped in prophase I of meiosis I, and are called primary oocytes. They lie within the ovaries surrounded by other cells, the follicular cells. The primary oocyte plus its follicular cells comprise the primary follicle.

At puberty, each oocyte enters meiosis again, just before it is ready to be ovulated. This means some oocytes can remain dormant for up to 50 years. FSH and LH act on a primary follicle in the ovaries, promoting its development into a secondary follicle.

The secondary follicle will continue to develop, and eventually forms a mature ovarian follicle called a tertiary, or Graafian, follicle. Once this mature follicle has developed, the further rise in oestrogen leads to a surge in LH (and some FSH), which stimulates ovulation.

The ovum (surrounded by its zona pellucida and cumulus of granulosa cells) will burst out of the follicle, ovulated and free to travel towards the uterus, hoping to meet a sperm cell on the way.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In human female, second polar body is formed in the ovum
questions.solution: During oogenesis, the primary oocyte undergoes meiosis I to form the secondary oocyte and the first polar body during the formation of the Graafian follicle. This occurs in the ovary. This secondary oocyte is released during ovulation and reaches the fallopian tubes (oviducts). Fertilization occurs here. When the sperm enters the ovum, the secondary oocyte undergoes the second meiotic division to release the second polar body. Also, the first polar body at the same time completes second meiotic division to form two secondary polar bodies.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The steps involved in spermatogenesis are given below. Arrange them in proper sequence and select the correct option.

A. Primary spermatocytes undergo the first meiotic division.
B. Spermatogonia multiply by mitotic division.
C. Transformation of spermatids into sperms.
D. Secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division.
E. Release of sperms from the seminiferous tubules.
questions.solution:
The process of spermatogenesis is as follows:

1. Spermatogonia present in seminiferous tubules multiply by mitotic division and increase in numbers.

2. Few spermatogonia called 'primary spermatocytes' undergo meiotic division to form two equal 'secondary spermatocytes'.

3. Secondary spermatocytes undergo meiotic division to form four haploid spermatids.

4. Spermatids are transformed into sperms by the process of spermiogenesis.

5. Sperms are released from the seminiferous tubules by the process of spermiation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In humans, inhibin
options: inhibits the production of FSH from pituitary but doesn't inhibit the secretion of Gonadotropin Releasing hormone (GnRH) from the hypothalamus.
doesn't inhibit the production of FSH from pituitary but inhibits the secretion of Gonadotropin Releasing hormone (GnRH) from the hypothalamus.
inhibits the production of FSH from pituitary as well as the secretion of Gonadotropin Releasing hormone (GnRH) from the hypothalamus.
neither inhibits the production of FSH from pituitary nor does it inhibit the secretion of Gonadotropin Releasing hormone (GnRH) from the hypothalamus.
questions.solution: In males, hormone inhibin produced by Sertoli cells inhibits the production of FSH from the pituitary. However, inhibin does not inhibit the secretion of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) from the hypothalamus. In females, inhibin is produced by granulosa cells of the ovarian follicles. Androgens stimulate inhibin production, while GnRH inhibits inhibin production.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are the steps involved in parturition. Arrange them in proper sequence and select the correct option.

I. The induction of mild uterine contractions is called foetal ejection reflex.
II. Stronger uterine contractions causing the further release of oxytocin.
III. Origination of signals from the fully developed foetus and placenta.
IV. Release of oxytocin from maternal pituitary
V. Expulsion of baby from the birth canal
questions.solution:
The steps involved in parturition are as follows:

1. The fully developed foetus and the placenta give rise to signals for parturition.

2. This induces mild uterine contractions known as foetal ejection reflex.

3. This stimulates the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary.

4. The uterine contractions keep getting stronger which causes further release of oxytocin.

5. The simultaneous uterine contractions and release of oxytocin finally causes the expulsion of the baby from the birth canal.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Identify the structures labelled as A and B.
questions.solution:
The spermatogonia (sing. spermatogonium) are present on the inside wall of seminiferous tubules, and they increase in numbers by mitotic division. Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains 46 chromosomes.
Some spermatogonia are called primary spermatocytes, which undergo meiotic division. They form second spermatocytes, which divide meiotically and give rise to haploid spermatids. They transform into spermatozoa (sperms) by the process called spermiogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The cluster of cells responsible for secreting milk is present in the
questions.solution: The mammary glands are paired structures (breasts) that contain glandular tissue and a variable amount of fat. The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15–20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. The cells of alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of alveoli. The alveoli open into mammary tubules. The tubules of each lobe join to form a mammary duct. Several mammary ducts join to form a wider mammary ampulla, which is connected to lactiferous duct through which milk is sucked out.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements regarding fertilization and implantation are incorrect?

I. During fertilization, a sperm first comes in contact with the corona radiata cells produced by the ovum.
II. Fertilization occurs only if sperm and ovum are simultaneously transported to the ampullary region.
III. Implantation occurs about 7 days after fertilization.
IV. The continuous division of morula leads to the formation of zygote.
questions.solution:
I. Corona radiata cells are not produced by the ovum. They are produced by the ovary which forms the follicle around the ovum.

II. Fertilization is the process of the union of sperm and ovum, which leads to the formation of zygote. This occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube. The sperm is viable for a period of 24-48 hours and an ovum is viable for a period of 24 hours. Therefore, for fertilization to occur, it is necessary that the sperm and ovum are transported simultaneously to the ampullary region.

III. Implantation is the process by which the blastocyst gets embedded in the endometrium. It occurs about 7 days after fertilization.

IV. The continuous division of morula leads to the formation of blastocyst. The blastocyst then further moves towards the uterus for implantation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding female reproductive system is incorrect?
options: Oviducts, uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts.
The narrowest part of the oviduct is the ampulla.
The uterus opens into the vagina through a narrow cervix.
Mons pubis is a cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair.
questions.solution:
I. The female accessory ducts are constituted by the oviducts, i.e., fallopian tube, uterus and vagina.

II. The ampulla is the widest part of the oviduct. It is the part where sperm and ovum are transported simultaneously by the fimbriae. Union of sperm and ovum, i.e., fertilisation occurs in this part.

III. The uterus opens into the vagina through a narrow cervix. The cavity of the cervix is known as the cervical canal.

IV. Mons pubis is a part of the female external genitalia. It is a cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statement is not correct about spermatogenesis?
options: Spermatogonia multiply by mitotic division and increase in number
Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains 46 chromosomes
A primary spermatocyte completes first meiotic division leading to formation of two equal haploid cells called secondary spermatocyte
questions.solution: In testis, the immature male germ cells (spermatogonia) produce sperms by spermatogenesis that begins at puberty. The spermatogonia (sing. spermatogonium) present on the inside wall of seminiferous tubules multiply by mitotic division and increase in numbers. Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains 46 chromosomes. Some of the spermatogonia called primary spermatocytes periodically undergo meiosis. A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to the formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes, which have only 23 chromosomes each. The secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following cells produce factors that help in maturation of spermatids to spermatozoa?
questions.solution:
Sertoli cells of a seminiferous tubule of testis secrete inhibin, a proteinaceous hormone, when sperm count is too high. This hormone causes negative feedback to suppress the overactivity of the FSH hormone to suppress spermatogenesis.

Also, FSH acts on the sertoli cells and stimulates the secretion of some factors which help in the process of spermiogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology

Read the following statements carefully.

1. Female external genitalia include labia majora, labia minora, clitoris, vagina, and hymen.
2. In females, at puberty, both ovaries contain about 60,000-80,000 primary follicles.
3. The progesterone hormone concentration remains high prior to ovulation in the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle.
4. The second meiotic division of secondary oocyte is completed inside ovary only after the entry of sperm.

​Female external genitalia include the mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, clitoris and hymen.

At puberty, each ovary contains 60,000-80,000 primary follicles. The estrogen hormone concentration remains high in the follicular phase prior to ovulation.

The second meiotic division of secondary oocyte completes inside fallopian tube only after the entry of sperm.

The estrogen hormone concentration remains high prior to ovulation in the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle.

options: responsible for the transportation of gametes.
responsible for the formation of androgens.
the site where sperms are produced.
the site where defective sperms are destroyed.
questions.solution: The 1-3 coiled structures present within the testicular lobules are known as seminiferous tubules. The process of formation of sperms i.e. spermatogenesis occurs here. These tubules are lined by two types of cells: male germ cells, i.e., spermatogonia, which develop into sperms and sertoli cells which provide nutrition to the sperms.

questions.q: Each of the following statements concerning the seminiferous epithelium is correct except.
options: It consists of Sertoli cells and spermatogenic cells
It has a robust basement membrane
questions.solution: It consists of a population of Sertoli cells and a spermatogenic cell line. Sertoli cells span the thickness of the seminiferous epithelium. Sertoli cell characteristics including the distribution of their intercellular junctions, divide the seminiferous epithelium into a basal compartment containing only spermatogonia and an adluminal compartment containing primary and secondary spermatocytes, spermatids, and spermatozoa. The differentiation of spermatogonia into spermatids does not begin until puberty. Thus, the seminiferous epithelium does not contain spermatids prior to puberty like all epithelial layers, the basal surface of the seminiferous epithelium is bounded by the basement membrane.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
How many is/are an incorrect matches in the following?

(1) Menopause: Cessation of menstruation in primate females.
(2) Cleavage: Rapid meiotic cell division occurs inside the fallopian tube.
(3) Spermiation: Release of sperms from the epididymis to penile urethra.
(4) Implantation: The embedding of blastocyst to the myometrium of the uterus which leads to pregnancy.
questions.solution:
Cleavage: Rapid mitotic cell division of zygote in the fallopian tube.

Spermiation: Releasing of sperms from the head of Sertoli cells to lumen of seminiferous tubules.

Implantation: The embedding of the blastocyst to the endometrium of the uterus which leads to pregnancy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following will have the same ploidy level?
options: Primary spermatocyte, primary oocyte, and second polar body
Oogonia, primary oocyte, and first polar body
Second polar body, spermatids, and primary spermatocyte
First polar body, secondary oocyte, and spermatozoa
questions.solution:
In human females, during oogenesis, the diploid structure with 46 chromosomes 44+XX is oogonium, which divides mitotically and gives rise to the primary oocyte (2n). Secondary oocyte, first and second polar body and ovum are produced as a result of meiotic division, and hence, they are haploid in nature.

In human males, during spermatogenesis, in the diploid structure with 46 chromosomes, 44+XY is spermatogonium, which grows in size and volume and produces to the primary spermatocyte (2n). Secondary spermatocyte, spermatids and spermatozoa are produced as a result of meiotic division and spermiogenesis; hence, they are haploid in nature.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Formation of acrosome is the function of
questions.solution: Acrosome is present on sperm head and consists of hydrolytic enzymes. These hydrolytic enzymes help in degradation of membrane of ovum during fertilization. Acrosome consists of enzymes processed by Golgi body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Each of the following statements concerning testosterone is true, except
options: It is synthesized by Leydig cells.
It is required for secondary development in males.
It is excluded from the adluminal compartment of the seminiferous epithelium.
questions.solution: Testosterone is the primary male sex steroid. It is an androgenic steroid synthesized by interstitial Leydig cells in the testes. It is required for spermatogenesis, functional differentiation of the excurrent ducts of the testes and the development of male secondary sexual characteristics. Androgen-binding protein synthesized by Sertoli cells assures that a high concentration of testosterone is present in the adluminal compartment of the seminiferous epithelium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following hormones is produced only during pregnancy?
questions.solution: The placenta acts as an endocrine tissue and produces several hormones like human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogens, progestogens, etc. In the later phase of pregnancy, a hormone called relaxin is also secreted by the ovary. Let us remember that hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced in women only during pregnancy. In addition, during pregnancy, the levels of other hormones like estrogens, progestogens, cortisol, prolactin, thyroxine, etc., are increased by several folds in the maternal blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What are the structures on which progesterone acts?
questions.solution: The primary action of progesterone hormones is to regulate the development and function of the uterus. It also causes the proliferation of mammary stem cells in the breast. It shortens the cervix and thereby avoids premature birth.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The pore of gastrula is called
questions.solution: Gastrulation is the process by which a blastula converts into gastrula. During gastrulation, a three-layered embryo made of ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm enclosing a new cavity, called archenteron, is formed. The lumen of the archenteron forms the future gut, which opens outside through the blastopore. In protostomes, the blastopore becomes the mouth, and in deuterostomes, the anus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The cleavage of zygote begins in
questions.solution: Cleavage is the repeated mitotic division of zygote to form a solid ball of cells called morula, which later changes into a hollow ball of cells called blastula.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The hormone which stimulates the 'let down' release of milk from mother's breast when the baby is suckling is
questions.solution: Oxytocin hormone is secreted by posterior pituitary gland. It helps in the ejection of milk from mother's breasts, when the baby is sucking.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: An inverted pear-shaped organ attached to the pelvic wall involved in reproduction is
questions.solution: The uterus is a female reproductive organ located between the bladder and rectum, in the pelvic area, and is an inverted pear-shaped structure. The uterus is connected to the fallopian tubes, the cervix, and the vagina. The main purpose of the uterus is to nourish a foetus prior to birth. In menstruating females, the ovaries release eggs that travel via the fallopian tubes to the uterus. If fertilized, the eggs bind themselves to the wall of the uterus (womb) and the foetus develops.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the correct statement regarding the menstrual cycle.
options: A rapid secretion of FSH leads to the rupture of the Graafian follicle and the ovum is released.
Estrogen secreted by the corpus luteum is necessary for the maintenance of the endometrium.
During the follicular phase, the primary follicles change into the Graafian follicle, which is transformed into corpus luteum post ovulation.
questions.solution:
During the follicular phase, the primary follicles in the ovary grow to become a fully mature Graafian follicle and simultaneously the endometrium of uterus regenerates through proliferation.
Ovulation is followed by the luteal phase where the Graafian follicle is transformed into corpus luteum.
Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle, and thereby, the release of the ovum.
The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which is essential for the maintenance of the endometrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these interactions between hormones of menstrual cycle is correct?
options: Estrogen has an inhibitory effect on the release of LH but a stimulatory effect on the release of FSH
Estrogen has an inhibitory effect on the release of FSH but a stimulatory effect on the release of LH
Progesterone has an inhibitory effect on the release of LH but a stimulatory effect on the release of FSH
Progesterone has an inhibitory effect on the release of FSH but a stimulatory effect on the release of LH
questions.solution: FSH causes the development of Graafian follicle which releases estrogen. Estrogen regulates the action of FSH by a negative feedback action. Increase in the blood concentration of estrogen stimulates the pituitary to release LH (LH surge) to cause ovulation. After ovulation LH causes the development of corpus luteum which releases progesterone. Progesterone regulates the action of LH by a negative feedback action. As long as progesterone is high a new cycle doesn't begin. It prevents release of FSH by the pituitary.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: hCG is produced by
questions.solution: The human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) hormone is a chemical messenger produced by cells formed after embryo development and implantation. These cells are produced by syncytiotrophoblasts of placenta and activate corpus luteum to produce progesterone. The presence of this hormone is a confirmatory test for positive pregnancy as this hormone is produced only during the gestation period.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the final stage of sperm maturation known as?
questions.solution: The final stage of sperm maturation is known as capacitation. This process is required for the process of fertilization and it occurs only after the sperm contacts the oocyte in the female reproductive tract.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following layer of uterus exhibits strong contraction during delivery of the baby?
questions.solution:
Perimetrium: outermost thin membranous layer of uterus.

Myometrium: Middle thick layer of smooth muscle which exhibits strong contraction during parturition.

Endometrium: Innermost glandular and vascular layer that lines the uterine cavity, undergo cyclic changes during menstrual cycle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following cells of blastocyst acts as a precursor of the embryo?
questions.solution: Cleavage of zygote results in the formation of a  64  celled stage called Blastocysts, which contain outer group of cells called Trophoblasts and inner group of cells called Inner cell mass, which gets differentiated as the embryo.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The oogonial cells start dividing and enter into __A__ of meiotic division and get temporarily arrested at that stage, called __B__. During oogenesis at puberty, this oocyte gets surrounded by granulosa cells and then called __C__.
options: A–Metaphase II; B–Primary oocyte; C–Primary follicle
A–Prophase I; B–Primary oocyte; C–Primary follicle
A–Prophase I; B–Secondary oocyte; C–Secondary follicle
A–Prophase II; B–Secondary oocyte; C–Secondary follicle
questions.solution: During embryonic development in females, the oogonia enter meiosis I and get halted in the pachytene stage of the prophase I (the most prolonged phase of the cell cycle) and are called a primary oocyte. During puberty, the halted meiosis I continue and forms the secondary oocyte and starts meiosis II that stops at metaphase II. In the course of development, the primary oocyte is surrounded by granulosa cells, which release estrogen and is called a primary follicle. During puberty, primary follicle matures and forms the Graafian follicle from which ovulation occurs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The seminal fluid coagulates on ejaculation due to
options: calcium and fibrinogen contents from prostatic and seminal vesicles secretions, respectively.
questions.solution: The action of clotting enzyme (of prostate) over fibrinogen (of seminal vesicles) changes the semen into a coagulum in vagina.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Find the odd one out with respect to hormones secreted by placenta.
questions.solution: <math><mtext>hCG, hPL,</mtext></math> estrogens and progestogen hormones are produced by the placenta in women only during pregnancy. Oxytocin is released by the maternal pituitary gland (neurohypophysis) at the time of childbirth due to fetal ejection reflex. Relaxin is produced by ovary only during pregnancy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below is a labelled diagram of the mammary gland, of which some parts are labelled as A, B, C and D.
Based on these labels, choose the part that contains the cluster of cells which secrete milk.
questions.solution:
A - mammary lobe
B - mammary duct
C - lactiferous duct
D - areola

The mammary glands are paired structures (breasts) that contain glandular tissue and a variable amount of fat. The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15-20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. The cells of alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of alveoli. The alveoli open into mammary tubules. The tubules of each lobe join to form a mammary duct. Several mammary ducts join to form a wider mammary ampulla which is connected to lactiferous duct through which milk is sucked out.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A woman had an extreme premature delivery. She gave birth to a baby boy at <math><mn>23</mn></math> weeks of gestation. The birth weight of the baby was <math><mn>950</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> . Which of the following is most likely to be observed in this baby?
options: The baby's heart will not be adequately formed
The baby's limbs and digits will not be adequately formed
The baby's external genitalia will not be adequately formed
The baby's eyelashes will not be adequately formed
questions.solution: The baby's heart forms after 4 weeks of pregnancy. The limbs and digits form at the end of 8 weeks. The external genitals form at the end of 12 weeks. As the baby was born at 23 weeks, these features will mostly be well developed in the baby. Features like body hair, separation of eyelids and formation of eyelashes complete at the end of 24 weeks. As the baby was born prior to it, most likely these features will not be adequately formed in the baby.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In case of mammals, testis are found in scrotal sacs outside the viscera because
options: of the presence of a long vas deferens.
of limited space due to the presence of urinary bladder.
questions.solution: In man, both testes normally remain suspended in a pouch called Scrotum outside the abdominal cavity. This keeps the testes at a cooler temperature than the body temperature (about 2°C below) this is essential for the maintenance and function of the spermatogenic tissue of the testes. Testes descend in the scrotal sac when fetus is about 7 month old and occurs under the influence of FSH and testosterone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The gestation period in humans is
options: 280 days from the end of the last menstrual cycle
280 days from the day of insemination
280 days from the day of fertilization of the egg
266 days from the day of the start of the last menstrual cycle
questions.solution: The fusion of a haploid male gamete (spermatozoan) and a haploid female gamete (ovum) to form a diploid zygote is called fertilization. In human females, fertilization is internal and it takes place in the ampulla of the fallopian tube. Fertilization occurs within 6 hours after ovulation. The condition of carrying one or more embryos in the uterus is called Pregnancy or Gestation. Human pregnancy lasts for an average of 266 days from fertilization of the egg or 280 days from the start of the last menstrual cycle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about morula in humans is correct?
options: It has almost equal quantity of cytoplasm as an uncleaved zygote but much more DNA.
It has far less cytoplasm as well as less DNA than in an uncleaved zygote.
It has more or less equal quantity of cytoplasm and DNA as in uncleaved zygote.
It has more cytoplasm and more DNA than an uncleaved zygote.
questions.solution: Morula is a solid ball contained within zona pellucida. It has almost equal quantity of cytoplasm as an uncleaved zygote but has much more DNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During the initial days of lactation, the milk produced is termed as
questions.solution: Lactation is the process of releasing milk from the breast which helps the mother to feed the baby. The initial milk secretion is called colostrum and it contains several antibodies important for resistance development in the baby.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The correct statement of cleavage in humans is
options: It is a process to convert zygote to gastrula.
It starts while the fertilized egg is in fallopian tube.
It is identical to normal mitosis.
It starts when the egg reaches the uterus.
questions.solution: Fusion of the sperm with the ovum is known as fertilization and it occurs at the ampullary-isthmic junction of the fallopian tube. The division of the zygote known as cleavage begins in the isthmus of the fallopian tube and the zygote moves towards the uterus while the division continues forming 2, 4, 8, 16 daughter cells called blastomeres. The zygote with 8-16 cells is called a morula. During cleavage the number of chromosomes in the daughter cells is same but the amount of cytoplasm is reduced. Hence it is not identical to mitosis

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In an average menstrual cycle of 28 days, which of these events is correctly matched with the time of its occurrence?
options: Endometrium secretes nutrients for implantation:15<sup>th</sup> -28<sup>th</sup> day
questions.solution:
The series of cyclic changes that take place simultaneously in the ovaries and uterine wall (endometrium) of the female reproductive tract stimulated by different concentrations of gonadotropins like FSH and LH is called the menstrual cycle. It is mainly made up of 4 phases:
Menstrual phase or Destructive phase -1st - 4th day - endometrium degenerate.
Proliferative phase or Follicular phase - 5th - 13th day - High F.S.H. level stimulates the primordial follicle to mature into the Graafian follicle.
Ovulatory phase - 14th day - the release of the ovum.
Luteal phase or secretory phase - 15th - 28th day - rise in progesterone levels and the endometrium secretes nutrients for implantation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements about male reproductive system and identify the correct ones.

I. The scrotum helps in maintaining the temperature ideal for spermatogenesis.
II. The male germ cells present in the seminiferous tubules undergo mitotic division and lead to the formation of sperms.
III. The bulbourethral glands secrete substances which help in lubricating the penis and these glands also help in formation of the ejaculatory duct.
IV. The site of spermatogenesis are highly coiled structures situated in the compartments of the testis.
questions.solution:
I. The scrotum is a pouch like structure in which the testis are suspended outside the abdominal cavity. It helps in maintaining the temperature 2-2.5 degree Celsius lower than internal body temperature, which is required for spermatogenesis.

II. The male germ cells present in the seminiferous tubules undergo meiotic division and lead to the formation of sperms.

III. The bulbourethral gland do not contribute to the formation of ejaculatory duct. The seminal vesicle contributes to it.

IV. The site of spermatogenesis is the seminiferous tubules. They are 1-3 highly coiled structures situated in the testicular lobules, which are the compartments of testis.

questions.subject: Zoology

options: Perimetrium - Outer thin covering of peritoneum
Myometrium - Middle thick smooth muscle layer

Endometrium - Inner glandular layer that lines the uterine cavity
questions.solution: The uterus is a part of the female reproductive system and is also known as the womb. It is an inverted pear-shaped organ that bears the foetus during pregnancy. The uterine wall has three layers which are perimetrium, myometrium, and endometrium. Perimetrium is the outer thin covering. Myometrium is the thick middle layer of smooth muscles and the inner layer which contains glands is called the endometrium. It is the endometrium that undergoes cyclical changes during menstrual cycle.

The structural and functional unit between developing embryo and maternal body is called placenta which is connected to the embryo through an umbilical cord.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on its head are usually observed during which month of pregnancy?
questions.solution: In human beings, after one month of pregnancy, the embryo's  heart is formed. By the end of the second month of pregnancy, the foetus develops limbs & digits. By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed. The first movements of the foetus & appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month. By the end of 24 weeks (second trimester), the body is covered with fine hair, eye-lids separate, and eyelashes are formed. By the end of nine months of pregnancy, the foetus is fully developed and is ready for delivery.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Several hormones like hCG, hPL, estrogen, progesterone are produced by
questions.solution:
Hormones secreted by the placenta are hCG, hPL, estrogen, and progesterone. Human chorionic gonadotropin hormone (hCG). This hormone is only produced during pregnancy almost exclusively in the placenta. HCG hormone levels found in maternal blood and urine increase dramatically during the first trimester and may contribute to causing nausea and vomiting often associated with pregnancy.

Human placental lactogen (hPL). This hormone, produced by the placenta, helps in the process of providing nutrition for the fetus and plays a role in stimulating milk glands in the breasts in anticipation of breastfeeding.

Estrogen. This group of hormones is responsible for the development of female sexual characteristics. Normally formed in the ovaries, estrogen is also produced by the placenta during pregnancy to help maintain a healthy pregnancy.

Progesterone. This hormone is produced by the ovaries and by the placenta during pregnancy. Progesterone stimulates the thickening of the uterine lining in anticipation of implantation of a fertilized egg.

The adrenal medulla is derived from ectoderm and it produces epinephrine and norepinephrine which are catecholamines. The pancreas is derived from endoderm and it produces insulin and glucagon which are peptide hormones. The parathyroid gland is derived from endoderm and it produces a polypeptide hormone called parathormone or Collip's hormone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are the steps involved in oogenesis. Arrange them in proper sequence and select the correct option.

1. Formation of primary follicle due to development of granulosa cells.
2. Division of oogonia and formation of the primary oocyte.
3. Formation of follicles having antrum.
4. Formation of secondary follicles.
5. An unequal division leading to the formation of secondary oocyte i.e. ovum and the first polar body.
questions.solution:
The sequence of oogenesis (formation of ovum) is as follows:

Millions of oogonia are added in a female fetal ovary after birth. These oogonia undergo division and lead to the formation of primary oocytes. A layer of granulosa cells surrounds these oocytes, which leads to the formation of primary follicles. More and more layer of granulosa cells and a new theca surround these primary follicles which leads to the formation of secondary follicles A fluid filled cavity called antrum develops which leads to the formation of tertiary follicle. An unequal division of the tertiary follicle leads to the formation of a haploid secondary oocyte i.e. ovum and a tiny first polar body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In human males urethra has
questions.solution: In human males urethra is around  <math><mn>20</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>  long. About  <math><mn>2.5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>  of urethra lies in the prostate (prostatic urethra), about  <math><mn>2.5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>  of urethra lies between prostate gland and penis (membranous urethra) and about  <math><mn>15</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>  of urethra lies in the corpus spongiosum of penis (penile urethra or spongy urethra). The prostatic urethra is connected to urinary bladder and is internally lined by transitional epithelium or urothelium. The major part of urethra (membranous and penile) has pseudostratified non-ciliated columnar epithelium. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are incorrect?

1. The longest phase of the menstrual cycle is the follicular phase while the shortest phase is the ovulatory phase.
2. When blastulation occurs, the uterus is the luteal phase with a well-developed endometrium
3. The formation of the haploid second polar body occurs just before ovulation.
4. Permanent cessation of menses is an indication of pregnancy.
questions.solution: The longest phase of menstrual cycle is luteal phase (around 13 - 14 days) while the shortest phase is ovulatory phase (around 1 day). The formation of haploid second polar body occurs just after ovulation within the fallopian tube once the sperm touches the ocum. Permanent cessation of menses is menopause. In preganancy menses stops temporarily and is regained after delivery of the child. Blastulation occurs within 4-5 days after fertilization. Fertilization aoccurs within two days after ovulation. So blastulation occurs within 7 days from ovulation when the uterus is still in the luteal phase

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The correct pathway of milk ejection from mammary glands is

(i) Sensory impulses are transmitted through somatic nerves from the nipples to the mother's spinal cord and then to her hypothalamus.
(ii) Expulsion of milk from alveoli into the ducts.
(iii) Suckling action of baby on the breast.
(iv) Contraction of myoepithelial cells.
(v) Secretion of oxytocin.
questions.solution: The mechanism by which milk is transported from the breast alveoli to the nipple is called milk ejection reflex. Suckling pf nipples by the baby Sensory impulses are transmitted through somatic nerves from the nipples to the mother's spinal cord and then to her hypothalamus (paraventricular nuclei and supraoptic nucleus). They send signals to the posterior pituitary gland to produce oxytocin. Oxytocin stimulates contraction of the myoepithelial cells surrounding the alveoli, which already hold milk. The increased pressure causes milk to flow through the duct system and be released through the nipple. This response can be conditioned e.g. to the cry of the baby.

questions.q: From which embryonic structure develops the vertebral column
questions.solution: The notochord develops into the vertebral column in vertebrates. The notochord lies along with the anteroposterior ("head to tail") axis, closer to the dorsal surface of the animal. Notochord is composed of cells derived from the mesoderm.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:

options: Release ovum from the Graafian follicle
Make necessary changes in the endometrium for implantation
Help in the development of corpus luteum
Help in the collection of the ovum after ovulation
questions.solution:
A - ovary
B - fimbrae 
C - uterus
D - fallopian tube

Fallopian tube (oviduct, uterine tube) is either of a pair of tubes that conduct ova (egg cells) from the ovary to the uterus. The ovarian end opens into the abdominal cavity via a funnel-shaped structure with a finger-like projection (fimbriae) surrounding the opening. Movements of the fimbriae at ovulation assist in directing the ovum to the Fallopian tube.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect about menstruation?
options: At menopause in the female, there is especially abrupt increase in gonadotropic hormones
The beginning of the cycle of menstruation is called menarche
During normal menstruction about 40 ml blood is lost
The menstrual fluid can easily clot
questions.solution:
Normal menstrual blood does clot, menstrual blood contains not only blood but also tissue from the lining of the uterus.
The female body typically releases anticoagulants to keep menstrual blood from clotting as it's being released. But when the period is heavy and blood is being rapidly expelled, there's not enough time for anticoagulants to work. That enables clots to form.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: All the following are the features of inhibin hormone, except:
options: Its secretion increases with increase in the number of spermatozoa.
It stimulates FSH secretion in males
It is secreted by Sertoli cells
questions.solution: Sertoli cells produce a glycoprotein called inhibin. lnhibin suppresses FSH synthesis by anterior pituitary and GnRH synthesis by hypothalamus. Thus normal release of testosterone is under negative feedback control.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following blocks the entry of additional sperm, once a single sperm cell encounters ova?
questions.solution: The zona pellucida (ZP) is an important, integral structure for the egg both before and after fertilization. The zona pellucida (ZP) is a name given to a clear (lucid) zone or region that surrounds the unfertilized egg and works to keep out the additional sperm that hangs around after the first union. It even stays close to the developing cells after fertilization to help out along the road to implantation in the uterus or womb.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution:

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: All the events of the menstrual cycle stop and there is no menstruation during pregnancy is due to
questions.solution: After fertilization the corpus luteum and later on placenta also secretes large amount of progesterone which is essential to maintain endometrium for implantation and other pregnancy conditions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements regarding fertilization is/are correct?

(i) The acrosome is filled with hydrolytic enzymes which help in dissolving the membrane of the ovum at the time of fertilization.

(ii) Vitelline membrane is the first membrane to be faced by sperms while trying to fuse with the ovum.

(iii) There must be synchronicity in the release of ovum and entry of sperm for the formation of zygote.

(iv) The meiotic division of the secondary oocyte is concluded with the entry of male gamete.
questions.solution:
During fertilization for the entry of sperm in the ovum, the acrosome breaks it with the help of digestive enzymes present in it. The acrosome contains hyaluronidase and acrosin enzymes which eat up the zona pellucida and allows the haploid nucleus in the sperm to join with the haploid nucleus of the ovum.

The outer membrane of the ovum is called Zona pellucida.

Egg can only survive for up to 24 hours after it's released while sperm can live in the female reproductive tract for about 3 to 5 days. Meeting of sperm with ovum in this duration can increase the chances of fertilization.

In oogenesis, oogonium(2n) undergoes mitosis and develops into a primary oocyte, which will begin the first meiotic division, but then arrest; it will finish this division as it develops in the follicle, giving rise to a haploid secondary oocyte and a smaller polar body.

The secondary oocyte begins the second meiotic division and then arrests again; and will remain so unless it is fertilized by a sperm; if this occurs, a mature ovum and another polar body is produced.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The first meiotic division during spermatogenesis takes place when:
options: Primary spermatocytes divide to form secondary spermatocytes
Secondary spermatocytes divide to form spermatids
Spermatogonia divide to form primary spermatocytes
questions.solution:
Spermatogenesis is a highly specialized process of cellular differentiation resulting in the formation of functional spermatozoa. Spermatogenesis begins with a diploid spermatogonium in the seminiferous tubules, which divides mitotically to produce two diploid primary spermatocytes.

The primary spermatocyte then undergoes meiosis I to produce two haploid secondary spermatocytes.

The haploid secondary spermatocytes undergo meiosis II to produce four haploid spermatids.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these statements about decidua is false?
options: Decidua cells are enlarged, vacuolated endometrial cells filled with glycogen and lipids.
Decidua parietalis refers to the part of the decidua which gives rise to maternal part
Decidua capsularis refers to the part of the decidua which overlies the embryo and separates it form the uterine cavity.
These cells are called decidua because they are shed off during parturition
questions.solution:
Decidua is the changed enlarged endometrium due to effect of increasing progesterone levels in maternal blood which converts it into decidual cells. They are enlarged, vacuolated and filled with glycogen and lipids. The stored glycogen and lipid are the source of nutrition for the embryo till placenta takes up this function. It is shed off during childbirth - hence why the term is used, "decidua" having the meaning of falling away, as in the word deciduous. Parts of decidua are

1 Decidua basalis or decidual plate refers to the part where maternal part of placenta is to develop.

2 Decidua capsularis is that part of the decidua which overlies the embryo and separates it from the uterine cavity.

3 Decidua parietalis refers to the part of the decidua lining the rest of uterine cavity.

questions.subject: Zoology

It helps to regulate temperature of testis for spermatogenesis .

The scrotum is a sac of skin that hangs from the body at the front of the pelvis.

questions.subject: Zoology

options: The testes are situated outside the abdominal cavity
The male germ cells undergo mitotic divisions
The interstitial space of seminiferous tubule contains Leydig cells which secrete testosterone
questions.solution:
Testicle or testis (plural testes) is the male reproductive gland or gonad in all animals, including humans. It is homologous to the female ovary. The functions of the testes are to produce both sperm and androgens, primarily testosterone.

Leydig cell which secrete testosterone and other androgens lies within the interstitial space of seminiferous tubule.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The figure shows a section of the human ovary. Select the option which gives the correct identification of A, B, C.



(i) A is a group of primary follicles that gradually matures under the influence of LH and FSH.

(ii) C is the Graafian follicle which starts producing a hormone called progesterone.

(iii) C is a corpus luteum that secretes FSH.

(iv) B is the Graafian follicle which ruptures during mid of the cycle.
questions.solution:
Corpus luteum, yellow hormone-secreting body in the female reproductive system that secretes progesterone which further maintains endometrium. Graafian follicle produce a hormone called estrogen by the follicular granulosa cells.

If fertilization does not occur, the corpus luteum involutes to form the corpus Albicans that is filled with fibrous tissue.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the components of human semen are correctly matched with the glands that secrete it?

(i) Citric acid - Prostate gland

(ii) Fibrinogen - Seminal vesicle

(iii) Prostaglandins - Prostate gland

(iv) Fructose - Seminal vesicle
questions.solution: Fluid from Seminal vesicle contains fructose, vitamin C, prostaglandins and fibrinogen. Fructose is a seminal fluid that provides energy to sperms. Prostaglandins increase the mobility of sperms and stimulate vaginal contractions, which help the infusion of gametes. Fibrinogen helps in the coagulation of semen after ejaculation. The prostatic fluid contains lipids citric acid, enzyme acid phosphatase and proteolytic enzymes. Proteolytic enzymes help in liquefaction of semen.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Human semen is liquid at ejaculation but it soon coagulates and then undergo secondary liquefaction under the influence of _______ secretion released by _______ gland.
questions.solution: The secretory product of prostate gland , which makes up part of the seminal fluid, is thin and milky, rich in citric acid, and hydrolytic enzymes, including fibrinolysin, which liquefies coagulated semen after deposition in the female genital tract

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Determine the incorrect statements regarding the process of female gamete production.

questions.solution: I. No more oogonia are added to the ovary after birth.III. The fluid filled cavity present in the tertiary follicle is called antrum.IV. The secondary oocyte forms a membrane called zona pellucida around it.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Hormones have the following features:

 I. Adenohypophysis produces gonadotropins
 II. Besides sex cells, hormones are also produced by testis and ovary
 III. Testosterone is produced by Leydig cells
 IV. Estrogen is produced by the ovary

 Which of the above factors influence secondary sexual characters?
questions.solution: Adenohypophysis or the anterior pituitary produces gonadotropins like LH and FSH, which triggers the gonads to produce the sex hormones progesterone, estrogen and testosterone. In females, progesterone, estrogen are responsible for controlling the menstrual cycle and also are responsible for the secondary sexual characters during puberty. In males, the testosterone produced by Leydig cells influences the spermatogenesis and secondary sexual characters.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The wrong statement about fertilization/ post fertilization changes in humans is
options: Fertilisation can occur only if sperm and ovum simultaneously reach the ampulla of the fallopian tube.
During fertilisation, the sperm comes in contact with the cell membrane of the ovum first.
The division of the morula leads to the formation of blastocyst.
The embryo is formed by the differentiation of inner cell mass.
questions.solution: During fertilisation, the sperm first comes in contact with the 'zona pellucida' layer of the ovum. Certain enzymes are released by the acrosome of the sperm. These enzymes cause certain changes in the zona pellucida layer. Thus, the entry of further sperms is prevented.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In which part of the sperm will we find a huge quantity of organelles nicknamed 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.solution: The middle piece of the sperm contains numerous mitochondria, the powerhouse of the cell. These mitochondria supply sperm with the energy, which it requires for its motility and fertilising capacity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following describes the function of the skin bag which encloses the testis?
options: It synthesises and secretes testicular hormones called androgens.
It provides nutrition to the germ cells.
It maintains the low temperature of the testes necessary for spermatogenesis.
It is made up of a special tissue that helps in erection of the penis to facilitate insemination.
questions.solution: The male gonads, the testes, lie outside the abdomen within the scrotum, which is a sac‐like structure derived from the skin and fascia of the abdominal wall. The scrotum helps in maintaining the low temperature of the testes (2–2.5°C lower than the normal internal body temperature) necessary for spermatogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If for some reason, the vasa efferentia in the human reproductive system gets blocked, the gametes will not be transported from
questions.solution: Vasa efferentia (Ductuli efferences) are 10-20 fine tubules which connect rete testis with an epididymis (Ductus epididymis). The latter is a pair of ducts from each testis which is formed by union of its vasa efferentia. If the vasa efferentia get blocked, the sperms will not be transported from testis to epididymis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Select correct statements related to the human female reproductive system

i. The wall of the uterus has three layers of tissue i.e., mesometrium, myometrium, and endometrium.
ii. The endometrium is the inner glandular layer that lines the uterine cavity.

questions.solution: The uterus has three layers the inner lining (endometrium) the middle muscular layer (myometrium) and the outer layer (perimetrium).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following structure of the female reproductive system can be taken as homologous to the scrotal sac of the male?
questions.solution: The external genitalia in females is known as the vulva. It consists of labia majora, labia minora, clitoris, mons pubis, the vestibule and vestibular glands. Labia majora is the pair of fleshy folds that extends from mons pubis to perineum. It is homologous to the male scrotum as both develop from same embryological tissue known as labioscrotal swellings.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the following statements about the human female reproductive system and identify the incorrect statement.
options: The wall of the uterus has three layers of tissue. The external thin membranous perimetrium, middle thick layer of smooth muscle, myometrium and inner glandular layer called endometrium that lines the uterine cavity.
The clitoris is a tiny finger-like structure which lies at the upper junction of the two labia majora above the urethral opening.
Each fallopian tube is about 10-12 cm long and extends from the periphery of each ovary to the uterus the part closer to the ovary is the funnel-shaped infundibulum.
The cavity of the cervix is called cervical canal which along with vagina forms the birth canal.
questions.solution: The female external genitalia include mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen and clitoris. options: Spermatogonia have 46 chromosomes and always undergo meiotic cell division.

questions.solution: Spermatogenesis is the formation of sperms that takes place in seminiferous tubules. It begins with growth phase of germ cells i.e. spermatogonia. These cells are formed in yolk sac and are transferred to testes. Spermatogonia being germ cells have 46 chromosomes and these undergo mitosis and growth to form primary spermatocytes. These then undergo meiosis-I to form secondary spermatocytes which then undergo meiosis-II to form spermatids. These spermatids then transform into spermatozoa and then sperms. Primary spermatocytes are formed due to mitosis and hence contain 46 chromosomes while secondary spermatocytes have 23 chromosomes.

questions.solution: The uterus is also called hystera or womb. It is an inverted pear-shaped structure. It is made up of three walls. The hormone causes uterine contractions during labor and helps shrink the uterus after delivery. When an infant suckles at his or her mother's breast, the stimulation causes a release of oxytocin, which, in turn, orders the body to "let down" milk for the baby to drink.

Read the statements given below :

(ii) Umbilical cord possess 100 percent foetal blood.

(iii) At puberty, in female each ovary contain about 60,000 - 80,000 primary follicles.

Choose the correct statement from the above
questions.solution: The baby movement called 'quickening', is sensed around 18-20 weeks of pregnancy. Umbilical cord possess 50% of foetal blood and 50% of maternal blood. The umbilical cord is a tube that connects the mother and the baby during pregnancy, with three blood vessels-one vein that carries food and oxygen in the maternal body from the placenta to the baby and two arteries that carry waste from the fetus/baby back to the placenta. The primary oocyte is surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells to form primary follicle and large number of these follicles degenerates during from birth to puberty. questions.solution: External genitalia in human females is known as Vulva. It consists of labia majora, labia minora, mons pubis and clitoris. It also has a vestibule which shows two openings. One is vaginal opening for menstrual flow, entry of penis and parturition. Other opening is urethral opening for outflow of urine. Thus there are two different openings in females unlike males. Hence the two systems: reproductive and excretory systems are separate systems and thus there is no shared duct between these two systems.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: How many ova and sperms will be produced from 100 secondary oocytes and 100 secondary spermatocytes during gametogenesis in a man?
questions.solution:
In oogenesis, one primary oocyte forms one secondary oocyte and one polar body. Secondary oocyte after second meiosis forms one mature ovum and one polar body. Thus 100 secondary oocytes will form 100 ova.

In spermatogenesis, one primary spermatocyte after first meiosis forms two secondary spermatocyte which undergoes second meiotic division to form four sperms. Thus 100 secondary spermatocytes will form 200 sperms.

questions.solution: Male reproductive system consists of accessory glands. These glands are seminal vesicles, prostate glands and bulbourethral glands. Secretions of these glands is seminal plasma and is rich in fructose, calcium and some enzymes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Polyspermy is prevented by all the events, except
options: Electrical changes in the egg membrane, depolarisation
Sodium gates in the egg membrane getting closed
questions.solution:
Although many sperm attaches to the egg, it is only one sperm enters into the egg. There are few mechanisms the animals adopt to ensure to avoid polyspermy. Among them the fast block to polyspermy is best studied.

Fast block to polyspermy occurs within a tenth of a second of fusion and involves the opening of Na+ channels in the plasma membrane of the egg. Na+ flows into the egg, by depolarizing the membrane and prevents additional sperm from fusing to the egg. 

The slow block to polyspermy starts within 10 seconds of fusion of the sperm and egg. Inositol triphosphate (IP3)  releases Ca++ from the endoplasmic reticulum and a wave of free Ca++ passes through the egg. This Ca++ results in the fusion of cortical vesicles with the egg plasma membrane, releasing their contents into the space surrounding the egg, called the perivitelline space. This raises the vitelline membrane and inactivates bindin receptors on the vitelline membrane. Thus, any additional sperm are released from the vitelline membrane and no more bind.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In human beings, the hollow ball of cells called a, about b days after fertilisation, burrows into the lining of uterus event called implantation. Blanks a, b respectively are
questions.solution: After the formation of the zygote, it enters the uterus in 3-5 days. n the uterus, the cells continue to divide, becoming a hollow ball of cells called a blastocyst. The blastocyst implants in the wall of the uterus about 7 days after fertilization.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The correct sequence of the arrangement of following parts in the mammary glands is
options: Mammary alveolus, mammary duct, ampulla and mammary lobe
Ampulla, mammary lobes, mammary alveolus and mammary ducts
Mammary lobes, mammary ducts, mammary alveolus and ampulla
Ampulla, mammary duct, mammary alveolus and mammary lobe
questions.solution: A functional mammary gland is characteristic of all female mammals. The mammary glands are paired structures (breasts) that contain glandular tissue and variable amount of fat. The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15-20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. The cells of alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of alveoli. The alveoli open into mammary tubules. The tubules of each lobe join to form a mammary duct. Several mammary ducts join to form a wider mammary ampulla which is connected to lactiferous duct through which milk is sucked out.

questions.solution: Placenta is a temporary organ which is formed during pregnancy inside the uterus. It is foetomaternal in origin. options: Facilitates supply of oxygen nutrients to embryo

questions.solution: The placenta is an important structure or organ which attaches the fetus to the mother's body through the umbilical cord. questions.subject: Zoology

options: Contribute to major part of semen
questions.solution: Sertoli cells are nurse cells or sustentacular cells present in the testes. These are present inbetween the spermatogonia. These cells are nurse cells as they provide nourishment to the developing sperms. Apart from this, they have many other functions. These cells also bring about release of Androgen binding protein (ABP) whch binds with the testosterone. These cells also form the blood testis barrier that helps to maintain luminal environment for sperm production. Semen is a mixture of Sperms and Secretions of accessory glands. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Reproductive organs in humans can be categorized into two categories primary and secondary. Which of the following is not a secondary sex organ?

a Prostate gland b Mammary gland c Seminal vesicle d Ovary
questions.solution: Reproductive organs in humans are divided into two categories: primary and secondary. Primary organs are those that form the sex cells i.e. sperms and ova. These are formed by testes in males and ovaries in females. These are collectively known as gonads. Hence gonads are considered primary sex organs. Apart from these structures, the remaining structures concerned with reproduction are secondary organs. These include the epididymis, vasa deferens, penis, urethra, ejaculatory duct, accessory glands like seminal vesicles, prostate glands and Cowper's gland in males. In females the secondary sex organs include oviduct, uterus, vagina, vulva, vestibular glands and mammary glands.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following structure is homologous to penis?
questions.solution: Penis in males is the main copulatory organ. It carries sperms and urine. It delivers sperms into the female body so that the sperms can fertilize the ovum. Penis is able to enter the female vagina because it is made up of three erectile tissues. These are two corpora cavernosa and one corpora spongiosum through which urethra passes. This erectile tissue becomes engorged with blood and thus the penis becomes hard and stiff. Such erectile tissue is seen in females too and is known as clitoris. The erectile tissue present is corpora cavernosa. Clitoris is present at the anterior junction of labia minora. Hence clitoris is homologous to the penis. Homologous organs are those organs that are similar in embryonic origin but different in function.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Testes consists of structural units known as Seminiferous tubules. These are present inside the lobules of testes. Each lobule consists of one to three such tubules in highly coiled manner. Seminiferous tubules consist of two cells. The main Spermatogonia i.e. mother cells that form the sperms and Sertoli cells or nurse cells that help to mature the sperms. These cells are present in between Spermatogonia. In between the seminiferous tubules is interstitial tissue that contains Leydig cells, Blood vessels, immune cells etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: At puberty, a female has more than 400,000 immature egg cells in her ovaries. Calculate the percentage of these eggs that will ovulate, assuming that 13 ovarian cycles occur per year in her reproductive life span of 40 years.
questions.solution: At the time of birth, there will be approximately 1 million eggs in the ovary of the female child. By the time of puberty, only about 300,000 remains and other undergo atresia. Around 300 to 400 only will be ovulated during a woman's reproductive lifetime. Hence, the percentage will be around 0.1 to 0.2.
