questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The first movements of the fetus are observed during
questions.solution: Human pregnancy lasts for nine months and it officially begins after implantation i.e.  <math><msup><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup></math>  day after fertilization. The sign of developing foetus is first recorded at the end of  <math><msup><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow></msup></math>  month as heart sounds are clear and audible. The foetus develops limbs and digits by the end of 60 days. Major systems also develop in the third month of pregnancy. The first movements of foetus and appearance of hair (known as Lanugo) on head is seen during fifth month.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which is wrong about oogenesis?
questions.solution: During oogenesis primary oocyte undergoes first meiotic division. This results in the formation of two daughter cells. These are secondary oocyte and a first polar body. These are unequal in size. Polar bodies are much smaller in diameter than the oocyte because the cytoplasm is retained in bulk in the secondary oocyte. This occurs because the secondary oocyte will get converted into ovum and if it gets fertilized will form zygote. Hence the retained cytoplasm will act as stored food for the developing zygote. This is the main difference between oogenesis and meiosis division in other cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In human male testes, the regions outside the seminiferous tubules are called interstitial spaces, and they contain
questions.solution: Testes consist of structural units known as seminiferous tubules that are present inside the lobules of testes. Each lobule consists of one to three tubules in a highly coiled manner. Seminiferous tubules comprised of two cells, the main spermatogonia i.e. mother cells that form the sperms and the Sertoli cells or nurse cells where the sperms mature. In between the seminiferous tubules is interstitial tissue that contains Leydig cells, blood vessels, immune cells etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The last part of the oviduct which has a narrow lumen and joins the uterus is
questions.solution: Female reproductive system consists of a pair of ovaries, oviducts, uterus, vagina, and cervix. The oviduct is also known as the Fallopian tube. It is further divided into three parts. The infundibulum is the first part of the oviduct that also has extensions known as fimbriae that collects ova from ovary. Second part is the ampulla and this is the widest part of oviduct. This is the region where the chances of fertilization is maximum. The last part is isthmus which finally opens into the uterus through opening called as cornua.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Identify the incorrect character related to the human female reproductive system.
options: Menstruation is repeated at an average interval of about <math><mrow><mrow><mn>28</mn></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mn>29</mn></mrow></mrow></math> days.
Menopause occurs around 50 years of age.
Ovulation occurs during the pregnancy period as well.
questions.solution: Menstrual cycle is the reproductive cycle in females. The word 'mesum' means one month. Hence this cycle is repeated every month the average interval being <math><mrow><mrow><mn>28</mn></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mn>29</mn></mrow></mrow></math> days. This cycle prepares the uterus every month to receive the fertilized product. But if the zygote doesn't arrive the endometrial lining along with ovum sheds and reforms for the next cycle. This continues every month till menopause is reached . Menopause is stoppage of cycle which is seen at the age of 45-52 years. This marke the end of fertility period in females. During menstrual cycle changes are seen in ovary and uterus simultaneously. This cycle begins with menstrual or bleeding phase which lasts for 3 to 5 days. The mid of the cycle (approximately) shows ovulation i.e. release of ovum from the ovary into the oviduct and here the ovum waits for the sperms to arrive. If sperms arrive fertilization might take place and this zygote will then be implanted in the uterus. If sperms does not arrive the ovum will degenerate and will be out through menstruation. Implantation marks the beginning of pregnancy which means zygote will develop for 9 months inside the uterus (in humans). During this period menstruation is not possible as endometrium shedding will cause embryo to shed too. Thus ovulation also does not take place during entire pregnancy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The ________X________ cells of testes secrete testosterone in ___________.

Choose the correct option for X and Y.
options: X: Sertoli cells; Y: Seminiferous tubules
questions.solution: The regions outside the seminiferous tubules interstitial spaces, which all interstitial spaces which contain interstitial cells or Leydig cells, which synthesise and secrete testicular hormones also called androgens in blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
In the following the duration of intra-uterine life is matched with the events completed. Which of these is matched correctly?

i. End of the first month: Embryo heart is formed
ii. End of the second month: Foetus develops limbs and digits
iii. End of the fifth month: Hair on head
iv. End of the sixth month: Eyelashes are formed
questions.solution: Human pregnancy lasts for nine months and it officially begins after implantation i.e. 8th day after fertilization.The sign of developing foetus is first recorded at the end of 1st month as heart sounds are cleary audible. The foetus develops limbs and digits by the end of 60 days. Major systems also develop in the third month of pregnancy.Hence as the first trimester (3 months or 12 weeks) is completed the foetus has developed organ systems and limbs and digits. The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month. By the end of 24 weeks (second trimester), the body is covered with fine hair, eye-lids separate, and eyelashes are formed.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which cells of the blastocyst are responsible for the development of the embryo and its extra-embryonic membranes, respectively?
questions.solution: Cleavage of zygote results in the formation of a 64 celled stage called Blastocysts, which contain outer group of cells called Trophoblasts and inner group of cells called Inner cell mass, which gets differentiated as the embryo.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a human female, if the duration of her menstrual cycle is of 34 days. What is the duration of the luteal phase and at what day ovulation occurs in this woman?
questions.solution:
Reproductive cycle of the primate female is called menstrual cycle. Among all three phases of menstrual cycle, the luteal phase or secretary phase is most constant, fixed and is duration of 14 days.

Day of ovulation in woman = (Total no. of days in menstrual cycle - 14)= 34 - 14 =20

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following organelles is absent in human sperm?
questions.solution: Human sperm consists of Head, Neck, Middle piece and Tail. Head consists of nucleus, chromosomes and it is covered by acrosome. Acrosomes contain enzymes that help in penetration of the ovum. These are modified Golgi apparatus. The neck consists of proximal and distal centrioles. Middle piece has 25-30 spirally arranged mitochondria which are the power houses of the cell. Thus sperm shows presenc of nucleus, centrioles and mitochondria but Endoplasmic reticulum is absent.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What would happen if vasa defferentia of man are cut?
questions.solution: Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of Testes, a pair of Epididymis, a pair of Vasa deferentia, Ejaculatory duct, Penis and Accesory glands. Testes are primary sex organs as they produce male sex cells i.e. sperms. These are produced inside the testes through process known as Spermatogenesis. These sperms from testes then enter the epididymis where they mature and attain motility. The sperms are then carried by vasa deferentia back into the abdomen through inguinal canal. These tubes then fuse with duct of seminal vesicles and form Ejaculatory ducts which then merges with urethra. Here seminal fluid from glands and sperms mix to form semen which is then ejaculated out. Thus if vasa deferentia are cut sperms will not be present in semen.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The function of ovary is

a To produce female gamete b To provide the site for fertilisation

c To provide the site for implantation d To produce several steroid hormones
questions.solution: Female reproductive system consists of Ovaries, Oviduct, Uterus, Vagina and Vulva. Oviduct is also known as fallopian tube. It is made up of three parts: Infundibulum, Ampulla and Isthmus. Infundibulum is funnel shaped part and extends as fimbriae which collects ova from ovary. Uterus is Hystera or Womb and is inverted pear shaped structure. Vulva consists of labia majora, Labia minora, Clitoris, Mons pubis and Vestibule. Ovaries are primary sex organs as these produce female gametes. These are also considered as Heterocrine glands as these secrete Hormones like estrogen, progesterone which are steroid hormones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not true for gastrula stage of embryonic development in human?
options: Formation of blastocyst with fluid filled cavity
Formation of three primary germinal layers
Formation of epiblast and hypoblast from germinal disc
questions.solution:
Due to cleavage, the zygote is changed to a 64-celled or blastomere stage called a blastocyst, has an outer layer of trophoblast cells, inner mass of cells, and a blastocyst cavity in blastula stage. This blastocyst is going to be implanted in the endometrium of the uterus in the presence of progesterone hormone.

Formation of gastrula from blastula is known as gastrulation. During gastrulation, three primary germinal layers-ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm are formed by morphogenetic movements and rearrangement of the cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mammary gland of a woman is
questions.solution:
The mammary gland of a woman is an exocrine gland having a duct system. Its secretion is called milk, which provides nutrition and immunity to newborn babies.

The mammary gland is a modified sweat or sudorific gland and an important reproductive organ in female.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following gland is homologous to Bartholin's gland and helps in lubrication of penis?
questions.solution: The male accessory glands include paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired (Cowper's glands) bulbourethral glands. Secretions of these glands constitute the seminal plasma which is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes. The secretions of bulbourethral glands also helps in the lubrication of the penis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not part of the vulva?
questions.solution:
Female external genitalia

- Mons pubis : It is the fatty tissue cushion which is covered by skin and pubic hair.

- There are 2 pairs of fleshy folds of tissue around vagina:

1. Labia majora (outer) : These extend down from the mons pubis surrounding the vagina.

2. Labia minora (inner) : These are located under the labia majora.

- Hymen

- It is the membranous structure partially covering the vagina.

- Presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity.

- Clitoris

- It is a small finger-like structure located at the upper meeting point of the two labia minora (just above the urethral opening).

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution:

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Absence of sperms in semen is called
questions.solution: Oligospermia means less number of sperms per ejaculate. Polyspermia means a large number of sperms than normal per ejaculate. Asthenospermia is a reduced motility of sperms. Azoospermia means the complete absence of sperms in semen.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The first meiotic division during oogenesis is completed at the stage of
options: primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle
questions.solution: Oogenesis is the process of formation of oocyte involving the process of folliculogenesis. Oogenesis begins before birth and the ovaries before birth consist of many primary oocytes. At birth these oocytes are surrounded by follicular cells and this is primary follicle. These remain in the ovary till puberty. As puberty is attained one oocyte completes its cycle. At the beginning primary oocyte is within primary follicle. Oocyte begins its Meiosis I and arrests at Prophase-I. Primary follicle then develops into secondary and further into tertiary follicle but the follicle remains in the arrested prophase-I phase. When tertiary follicle is formed the primary oocyte finally completes its meiosis I and forms secondary oocyte and first polar body after which the tertiary follicle forms the Graffian follicle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following cells of human testis are present in the regions outside the seminiferous tubules but in the testicular lobules?
questions.solution:
Each seminiferous tubule is lined on its inner side by two types of cells called spermatogonium/make germ cells and Sertoli cells/Nurse cells.

Leydig cells or interstitial cells are present in the region outside the seminiferous tubules of testes. These secrete testosterone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following reproductive structure is divided into cortex and medulla?
questions.solution:
Ovaries are the primary sex organs in female. Each ovary is covered by a thin epithelium which encloses the ovarian stroma. The ovarian stroma is divided into two zones- a peripheral cortex and an inner medulla.

Ovarian cortex contain large number of ovarian follicles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The main cause of the disintegration of the endometrial lining is
questions.solution: Menstrual cycle shows changes in ovary and uterus simultaneously. It begins with menstruation i.e. bleeding phase. It continues for five days. Menstruation means shedding of endometrial lining from uterus. This occurs due to decrease in levels of ovarian hormones: Estrogen and Progesterone. These hormones decrease because in the ovary the corpus luteum of previous cycle start disintegrating. Thus degeneration of corpus luteum causes the ovarian hormones to decrease and thus endometrium degenerates leading to bleeding phase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The Graafian follicle contains
questions.solution: The ovaries are the female reproductive organs where the ovarian follicles are found. Sometimes they are also called as Graafian follicles. The ovarian follicle is a fluid-filled sac which contains a primitive ovum or oocyte. During ovulation, there is a cyclical development in one or more of these follicles each month, which in turn releases a mature egg.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The secretions of the male sex accessory glands constitute the
questions.solution: The male accessory glands include the seminal vesicles, the prostate gland and the bulbourethral glands. These glands play a role in facilitating the transfer of sperms into the vagina during copulation. The seminal plasma is nothing but the fluid which has secretions from all the organs of the seminal tract and together with the sperms it forms the semen.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which event ensures that only one sperm can fertilize an ovum?
questions.solution: Block to polyspermy is an important step which takes place in humans (even in sea urchins) during fertilization. This is done by two events. Fast block to polyspermy takes place because of opening of sodium channels that cause the oocyte membrane to get depolarized. There is slow block to polyspermy too. This takes place due to cortical and zona reactions. These two types of block to polyspermy ensures that only one sperm can fertilise the ovum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following does not occur between 15-28 day of menstrual cycle?
questions.solution: Menstrual cycle consists of changes in the ovary and the uterus simultaneously. It begins with the menstrual or bleeding phase. This represents the shedding of the endometrium of uterus and unfertilized secondary oocyte. This phase is followed by the follicular phase as follicles start developing in the ovary. At the same time the shedded endometrium starts its preparation and this is termed as proliferative phase. The mid of 28-day cycle shows the ovulatory phase that is Graffian follicle from ovary releases secondary oocyte in the oviduct. This is followed by the formation of a corpus luteum and is known as Luteal phase. The secondary oocyte in the oviduct can undergo fertilization hence the uterus prepares itself to receive the fertilized egg by forming secretory glands i.e. secretory phase is seen. As no fertilization takes place the secondary oocyte now starts travelling towards the uterus to shed along with the endometrium i.e. new menstrual cycle begins.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The uterus open into vagina through a narrow
questions.solution: The female reproductive system consists of a pair of ovaries, a pair of oviducts, uterus, vagina, and vulva. The uterus is also known as the womb or hysteria. The parts of the uterus are fundus, body, and cervix. Cervix is between the body of uterus and vagina and this shows two openings internal and external os. Thus uterus opens into the vagina through cervix.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The scrotum helps in maintaining the low temperature of the testes, necessary for __________________.
questions.solution: The testes are situated outside the abdominal cavity within a pouch called scrotum. The scrotum helps in maintaining the low temperature of the testes (2–2.5°C lower than the normal internal body temperature) necessary for spermatogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The largest cell among the following is
questions.solution: Formation of zygote is universal in all sexual reproducing organism. Zygote is the first product of sexual reproduction which is formed by fusion of male gamete with egg cell or female gamete. Zygote undergoes cleavage which reduces the cell size. Every sexually reproducing organism, including human beings begin life as a single cell the zygote. Zygote is the vital link between organism of one generation and next as it undergoes division to form embryo from which new progeny develops.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Arrange the following events occurring in the ovary in the CORRECT sequence

a. The antrum is formed.

b. Formation of a first tiny polar body.

c. The primary follicle get surrounded by more and more layers of granulosa cells.

d. The primary oocyte is arrested in prophase-I of the meiotic division.
options: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></math>  and  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></math>  and  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></math>  and  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></math>
questions.solution: Oogenesis involves the development of oocyte and also folliculogenesis, which takes place in the Ovary. The primary oocyte develops first and begins its meiosis-I, which gets arrested at prophase-I. This stage is followed by the development of granulosa cells around it, known as primary follicle formation. The primary follicle then develops into the secondary follicle, which is characterized by the formation of the theca layer around granulosa cells. This then develops into the tertiary follicle. The differentiating feature is the formation of Antrum, which is initially crescent-shaped and later becomes large. This tertiary follicle still shows the presence of primary oocyte in it. These two then undergo further development. Primary oocyte completes its meiosis-I and forms two unequal cells: Large secondary oocyte and a small first polar body. Tertiary follicle further develops into Graffian follicle and secondary oocyte starts it meiosis-II.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In which stage does the embryo differentiate into trophoblast and an inner group of cells?
questions.solution: The blastocyst is a structure formed in the early development of mammals. It possesses an inner cell mass (ICM) which subsequently forms the embryo. The outer layer of the blastocyst consists of cells collectively called the trophoblast.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Testosterone is synthesized by
questions.solution: Testes are male gonads. These are present outside the abdominal cavity. The transverse section of the testes shows many lobules and each lobule consist of 1-3 seminiferous tubules. These tubules show the presence of two types of cells. Spermatogonia i.e. mother cells and Sertoli cells i.e. nurse cells that are present in between the spermatogonia. Spermatogonia form sperms while Sertoli cells nourish the sperms. In between the seminiferous tubules, there are present Leydig cells or interstitial cells that secrete male sex hormone testosterone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The second meiotic division of ________P________ is unequal and results in the formation of ______Q________.

Select the appropriate option for P and Q.
questions.solution: The entry of sperm into the cytoplasm of secondary oocytes brings the signal to induce the completion of the meiotic division. The second meiotic division of secondary oocyte is unequal which results in the formation of a large size haploid ovum and a tiny haploid cell called a polar body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Menstruation or menstrual flow in a woman occurs due to lack of hormone
questions.solution: Due to regression of corpus luteum the progesterone hormone concentration decreases which leads to degeneration and shedding off endometrium layer along with blood called menstruation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Blastocyst stage can be located in
questions.solution: Cleavage is the repeated mitotic division of zygote to form a solid ball of cells called morula which later changes into a hollow ball of cells called a blastula. The blastula gets attached to the uterus and is thus known as implantation.

questions.solution: Mons pubis is a cushion of fatty tissue that is covered by skin and pubic hair and more prominent in female. It provides cushioning during sexual intercourse. The labia majora are fleshy folds of tissue, which extend down from the mons pubis and surround the vaginal opening only. The labia minora form the two small folds of skin of the vulva. It lacks fatty tissue. The opening of the vagina is often covered partially by a membrane called hymen. The presence or absence of hymen is NOT a reliable indicator of virginity or sexual experience. Hymen is a very thin membrane that can be broken by exersion caused due to heavy exercise. The clitoris lies at the upper junction of two labia minora above the urethral opening. It is an erectile structure homologous to the male penis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: At  menopause there is rise in urinary excretion of:
questions.solution: Menopause is the time in a woman's life when monthly cycles of menstruation cease forever and the level of hormones (estrogens) produced by the ovaries decreases. Menopause usually occurs in the late 40s or early 50s. When estrogen production falls a critical value, estrogens can no longer inhibit the production of the gonadotropins. FSH and LH. Instead, the gonadotropins FSH and LH (mainly FSH) are produced after menopause in large and continuous quantities and these (mainly FSH) are excreted out in the urine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The difference between oogenesis and spermatogenesis is
options: oogenesis begins at puberty and spermatogenesis during embryonic development.
oogenesis results in formation of four haploid ova from a primary oocyte, while during spermatogenesis only one sperm is formed from a primary spermatocyte.
the cytoplasmic division is unequal in oogenesis and equal in spermatogenesis.
spermatogenesis is not completed until after fertilization occurs, but oogenesis is completed at the time of birth.
questions.solution: Oogenesis is formation of female gametes while spermatogenesis is formation of male gametes. Both begins with primary mother cells in the gonads. Primary oocyte undergoes meiosis 1 and forms secondary oocyte and first polar body while Primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis1 and forms two secondary spermatocyte. The process is the same in both but the daughter cells formed are different. In oogenesis, the daughter cells are of unequal size i.e. secondary oocyte is larger than the first polar body because secondary oocyte has maximum amount of cytoplasm retained in it. This unequal division is important because incase sperms approach these gametes, there is a chance of fertilization and zygote formation. Hence cytoplasm can act as stored food for the zygote. While in spermatogenesis the daughter cells formed are of same size as seen in Meiosis of other cells. This is the main difference.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The decrease in the number of sperms in semen is called ______X______and is due to the insufficient amount of ________Y_______. Select the correct option for X and Y.
questions.solution:
Oligospermia-It refers to fall or decrease the number of sperms in semen, which is mainly due to deficiency of male sex hormone testosterone. This leads to infertility in male.

Azospermia-This refers to absence of live sperms in semen.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The cells of the mammary gland that secrete and store milk are called
questions.solution: Mammary glands are accessory glands in females. These are milk producing glands. Each gland is divided into 15-20 lobes which are further divided into many lobules. Each lobule has grapelike clusters of milk secreting glands known as alveoli. Milk from alveoli then enters the tubules and finally into ducts. These are mammary ducts that enlarge near nipples and form ampullae. These are expanded structures as milk is stored here. These unite and form lactiferous ducts that finally open at the nipples. Pigmented area around the nipples is known as Areola and it consists of sebaceous glands. Adipose tissue or fatty tissue is found between the lobes and covers the surface of the gland. The amount of fatty tissue determines the size of the breast.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following antibody present in colostrum and provide passive immunity to the infant?
questions.solution: Active immunity means pathogen or antigen when introduced in the body triggers formation of antibodies. Passive immunity means directly antibodies are injected. It can be Natural or Artificial. Colostrum is the first milk produced by the mother after parturition. It is a rich of IgA and thus through this milk the antibodies are directly delivered to the baby. Thus this is an example of passive immunity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Birth canal is formed by
questions.solution: Female reproductive system consists of pair of ovaries, pair of oviduct, uterus, vagina and vulva. Uterus is also known as womb or hystera. The parts of uterus are fundus, body and cervix. Cervix is between the body of uterus and vagina and this shows two openings internal and external os. Embryo gets implanted in the uterus and develops into foetus within nine months following this parturition takes place. During parturition the foetus passes through cervix and vagina and hence these are together known as the birth canal.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Select the neuroendocrine process or mechanism from the mentioned reproductive events.

I. Parturition

II. Lactation

III. Menstrual cycle
questions.solution: Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism in which by fetal ejection reflex it triggers the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary. Lactation is also a neuroendocrine process in which after child birth, oxytocin is released to eject milk to feed the newborn. The menstrual cycle also is the neuroendocrine process which is dependent of the HPG axis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The luteal phase in the menstrual cycle of primate female is also called
options: secretory phase and lasts for about 13-14 days
follicular phase and lasts for about 6-7 days
proliferative phase and lasts for about 13-14 days
secretory phase and lasts for about 6-7days
questions.solution: The menstrual cycle has three important phases- (i) Follicular or proliferative phase, which lasts for about 7-9 days and is a highly variable phase. (ii) Ovulatory phase, the egg ruptures from the ovary on 14th day. (iii) Secretory phase, which lasts for about 13-14 days till the corpus luteum is survived and is the most constant phase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The trophoblast cells are not involved in the formation of
questions.solution: Trophoblast cells perform various functions such as provide protection, nutrition to inner mass cells, helps in implantation, forms chorionic villi that are fetal part of the placenta. The layer of trophoblasts after gastrulation, get formed into the trophectoderm, which in future forms the ectoderm of the embryo and gives rise to the organs that are derived from ectodermal layer.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In spermatogenesis reduction division of chromosome occurs during the conversion of
questions.solution: The germ cells in the seminiferous tubules giving rise to the haploid spermatozoa are known as spermatogenesis. The three stages involved in this process are mitosis, meiosis, and spermiogenesis. The first step begins when the stem cells start multiplying and produce duplicate cells(spermatogonia). When these cells mature they are known as primary spermatocytes which undergo meiotic-I cell division to form secondary spermatocytes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Release of the second polar body from human egg occurs
options: with no relation to sperm entry
questions.solution: During the process of oogenesis, the cells start dividing and there is a phase of temporary arrest where it forms the primary oocyte. These oocytes then form the primary follicles which degenerate during puberty. When these primary follicles get surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells they form the secondary follicle, which gets transformed into the tertiary follicle. When the tertiary follicle grows it undergoes first meiotic division and releases the first polar body and a secondary oocyte. The secondary oocyte then completes its second meiotic division and releases the second polar body after the entry of sperms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Identify the foeto-maternal organ
questions.solution: The placenta is also known as foeto-maternal organ because it is contributed by both foetus and mother. Placenta is formed in the uterus during pregnancy, creating a vital connection between the developing baby and the mother. It allows nutrient uptake, waste elimination, and gas exchange via the mother's blood supply.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Structure of human sperm is given. Identify the part which possess enzymes that help in fertilization.
questions.solution:
A = Acrosome, B = Nucleus, C = Mitochondria, D = Tail.

The sperm head possess :

Acrosome - It is a cap-like structure that covers the anterior portion of the head. It is filled with enzymes that help in fertilization of the ovum, like hyaluronidase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about the blastocyst?
options: Penetrates endometrium from its embryonic pole.
Consists of outer trophoblast and inner embryoblast.
Gets implanted along with zona pellucida.
Has a cavity called amniotic cavity.
questions.solution: The blastocyst is a hollow structure that contains a cluster of cells from which embryo arises. The outer layer provides placenta and other essential tissues for fetal development while the inner cells give rise to the tissues of the body. This outer layer is known as trophoblast which provides nutrients to the embryo. Embryoblast is cells which are situated within the trophoblast and result in the production of an embryo.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a functional breast, milk is temporarily stored in:
questions.solution:
Mammary glands

- 15 -20 mammary lobes are found in glandular tissue of each breast.

- Each mammary lobe is divided into numerous alveoli. Alveoli is a group of cells having a lumen within.

- Alveolar cells secrete milk in the lumen of alveoli where it is temporarily stored.

questions.solution: Menstrual cycle consists of changes in the Ovary and the Uterus simultaneously. It begins with Menstrual or bleeding phase. This represents shedding of endometrium of uterus and unfertilized secondary oocyte. This phase is followed by follicular phase as follicles start developing in the ovary. At the same time the shedded endometrium starts its preparation and this is termed as proliferative phase. At the same time the follicles develop in the ovary from day  <math><msup><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup></math>  to  <math><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup></math>  day.  The mid of 28 day cycle shows ovulatory phase that is graffian follicle from ovary releases secondary oocyte in the oviduct. This is followed by formation of corpus luteum and is known as Luteal phase and this shows high level of estrogen and progesterone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the correct statement:
options: The first movements of foetus and appearence of hairs on the head are usually observed during sixth month of pregnancy.
The mammary glands of the female undergo differentiation before puberty and start producing milk at the end of pregnancy.
Trophoblast cells contain specialised stem cells which have the potency to give rise all the tissue and organs.
After implantation, finger-like projection appears on the trophoblast which is surrounded by uterine tissue and maternal blood.
questions.solution:
The first movements of the fetus and the appearance of hairs on the head are usually observed during the fifth month of pregnancy.

The mammary glands of the female undergo differentiation during pregnancy and start producing milk towards the end of pregnancy.

Trophoblast cells provide nutrients to the embryo and develop into the placenta. They are formed during the first stage of pregnancy and become the first cells to differentiate into extraembryonic structures that do not directly contribute to the formation of the embryo.

After implantation, a finger-like projection called microvilli appear on the trophoblast which is surrounded by uterine tissue and maternal blood and is required for the supply of nutrients.

questions.solution: Pituitary hormones gonadotrophins i.e. FSH and LH control menstrual cycle in females. FSH is a follicle-stimulating hormone and its main function is to control the development and maturation of ovarian follicles. LH is luteinizing hormone that causes formation of corpus luteum after ovulation has taken place. Ovarian hormones progesterone and estrogen secreted by corpus luteum also play an important role in the menstrual cycle. Progesterone is also important as it prepares the endometrium for implantation by secreting secretory glands. Estrogen develops secondary sexual characters.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Extrusion of second polar body from egg nucleus occurs
options: after entry of sperm, before completion of fertilization
has no relation with sperm entry
questions.solution: In oogenesis the primary oocyte forms secondary oocyte just before ovulation. This secondary oocyte as formed starts Meiosis 2 but this is arrested at metaphase 2 and is ovulated at this stage. It enters the oviduct and remains viable for one day and then sheds in the form of menstruation alongwith the endometrial lining. Thus secondary oocyte sheds in the arrested phase only. When in the oviduct if the sperm enters there are chances of fertilization. The sperm swims the vagina, cervix and uterus are enters the oviduct where it approaches the ovum membrane. As the sperm touches the membrane the MAF (Metaphase arrested factor) disappears and thus Meiosis 2 completes following this, syngamy i.e. fusion of nuclei takes place and thus fertilization is completed.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which organ is oval in shape, has a dense covering, and lies in extra-abdominal pouch having two 2 to 1.5 degrees centigrade lower temperature than the body?
questions.solution: The testes - also called testicles - are two oval-shaped organs in the male reproductive system. They're contained in a sac of skin called the scrotum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Increase in temperature by <math><mn>2</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> of scrotum would
options: reduce the fertility by impairment of spermatogenesis
questions.solution: Spermatogenesis is the process of producing male gametes or sperms which will then participate in the fertilization process. This process requires lower body temperature and hence the testis is placed in the scrotal sac (scrotum) outside the lower abdomen. If the temperature of the scrotum is raises it will denature the enzymes required for the spermatogenesis process and reduce fertility as new sperms are not produced.

How many of the following structures are found in the primary sex organ of a male?

(I) The network of small tubules

(II) Leydig cells

(III) Blood vessels

(IV) Seminiferous tubules
questions.solution: The network of small tubules, blood vessels, seminiferous tubules, the interstitial cells of Leydig, are located in the connective tissue surrounding the sperm-producing tubules of the testes, are responsible for the production and secretion of testosterone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is FALSE?
options: Menarche is the beginning of menstruation.
Menstruation is the shedding of the endometrial lining.
Menopause occurs at the beginning of puberty.
Ovulation occurs under a high titre of LH.
questions.solution: The regular natural change occurring in the female reproductive system in a cyclical manner is called the menstrual cycle. This cycle helps in getting a female pregnant. Onsent of the menstrual cycle during puberty in a female is referred to as menarche. Menopause marks the end of the menstrual cycle phase in the life of the female. It usually occurs around the age of 43-45. Menstruation is the phase of menstrual cycle where the woman discharges blood and other material from the lining of the uterus. The endometrial lining is shed off. Ovulation is the phase of menstrual cycle where the mature ovum is released from one of the ovaries triggered by high surge of luteinizing hormone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Recognize the figure and find out the CORRECT matching.
questions.solution: Fertilization results in the formation of a zygote that takes place in the oviduct. This zygote then undergoes a series of changes before it actually gets implanted in the uterus. Zygote first undergoes cleavage and results in the formation of 16 cells known as a morula. This is a solid ball and is represented by <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>. The morula then enters the uterus and undergoes changes. The 16 celled morula further forms 32 cells and these then start arranging in two layers: outer trophoblast and inner embryonal mass. This also forms a cavity and is known as blastocyst and the structure is known as blastula. This now gets implanted in the uterus. Thus figure <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is blastocyst.

a-spermatozoa, b-spermatid, c-primary spermatocyte, d-secondary spermatocyte, e-spermatogonia, f-sertoli cell
a-spermatozoa, b-spermatid, d-primary spermatocyte, c-secondary spermatocyte, e-sertoli cell, f-spermatogonia
questions.solution: The testicular lobules which are the compartments in each testis contain highly coiled structures called the seminiferous tubules where the sperms are produced. The inner layer of the tubule is lined by male germ cells called the spermatogonia(f) and sertoli cells(e). These germ cells undergo meiotic divisions and produce and produce the primary spermatocyte(d) which again forms haploid cells called secondary spermatocyte(c). The secondary spermatocytes produce four haploid spermatids(b) by meiosis, these spermatids finally get transformed into spermatozoa(a).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following duct/ducts helps in the transportation of sperm and seminal plasma?
questions.solution: The male sex accessory ducts include rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens. The seminiferous tubules of the testis open into the vasa efferentia through rete testis. The vasa efferentia leave the testis and open into epididymis located along the posterior surface of each testis. The epididymis leads to vas deferens that ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder. It receives a duct from seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as the ejaculatory duct. These ducts store and transport the sperms from the testis to the outside through urethra. The urethra originates from the urinary bladder and extends through the penis to its external opening called urethral meatus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which hormone maintains progesterone and estrogen secretion by the corpus luteum through the first trimester of pregnancy?
questions.solution: After fertilization, the zygote undergoes a series of development and thus forms embryo. This embryo then gets implanted in the uterus at around the eighth day after fertilization and this marks the beginning of pregnancy. It is the blastula that gets implanted. The pregnancy can also be confirmed through blood or urine tests as hormone hCG (Human chorionic gonadotropin) begins to increase in blood and urine. This hormone begins to increase from the 8th day and remains in the blood till the parturition. Human chorionic gonadotrophin is the embryonic hormone that ensures the corpus luteum continues to produce progesterone throughout the first trimester of pregnancy. This hormone initially is released by trophoblast and then by placenta.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Cyclic menstruation is an indicator of the ____________ and extends between ________ and ____________.
questions.solution: Cyclic menstruation is an indicator of the normal reproductive phase and extends between menarche and menopause. In human beings, menarche starts at puberty and menstrual cycle ceases around 50 years of age; that is termed as menopause.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Find the INCORRECT statement about human reproduction.
options: Hormonal contraceptives are effective with lesser side effects and well accepted by females
Primary oocyte completes meiosis-I when sperm enters the cytoplasm of the primary oocyte
Spermatogenesis and oogenesis require different temperature
Spermatogenesis takes place in seminiferous tubules of testes
questions.solution: The primary oocyte completes the first reduction division in the tertiary follicle and results in the formation of the secondary oocyte. The completion of the meiotic division in the secondary oocyte takes place when the sperm enters the cytoplasm of the ovum. The second meiotic division which is unequal results in the formation of a second polar body and an ootid(haploid ovum).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Level of estrogen and progesterone are minimum at the time of
questions.solution: The menstrual cycle consists of changes in the ovary and the uterus simultaneously. It begins with the menstrual or bleeding phase. This represents the shedding of the endometrium of the uterus and unfertilized secondary oocyte. This occurs because the corpus luteum of the previous cycle is degenerating. Due to this the hormones secreted by corpus luteum also start decreasing. These hormones include estrogen and progesterone. These hormones are responsible for maintaining the uterine lining and since these are decreasing the uterine lining too starts shedding. Thus levels of these hormones are minimum at the beginning of the menstrual cycle. During the follicular phase, FSH is increasing and estrogen and progesterone have started the proliferation of the endometrium. During ovulation LH is at its peak and estrogen is also increasing. The secretory phase in uterus coincides with luteal phase in the ovary and thus because of the formation of corpus luteum, estrogen and progesterone are also high.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The embedding of _________X________ in the _________Y_________of uterus is called implantation. Select the correct option for X and Y.
questions.solution: The embedding of Blastocysts in the endometrium of uterus in the presence of progesterone hormone is called implantation. It occurs after 7th day of fertilization. Blastocyst is a 64-celled stage with a blastocoel cavity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The three phases of the uterine cycle in order are
questions.solution:
Menstrual cycle is the reproductive cycle in females. The name is derived from the word 'mesum' meaning one month. Thus this cycle is repeated every month. This cycle includes changes in the ovary and the uterus simultaneously.The beginning of the cycle is the bleeding phase also known as Menstrual phase. This continues for 3-5 days. During this phase there is shedding of endometrium and unfertilisedovum.This is followed by follicular phase in ovary which shows formation of new follicles and proliferative phase in the uterus that begins repair of endometrium. These phases are then followed by ovulation.Following this is the luteal phase in ovary that shows formation of corpus luteum and secretory phase in the uterus which shows formation of secretory glands as the uterus is preparing itself to receive the fertilised ovum. Fertilisation will mark the cessation of the cycle temporarily however if no fertilisation is seen the same cycle is repeated.Thus the phases are

Menstrual → Proliferative/Follicular → Ovulatory → Secretory/Luteal

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding menstrual cycle in females:

A. It is the reproductive cycle in all mammalian females.

B. The menstrual flow results due to breakdown of myometrium lining of uterus.

C. Graafian follicle and endometrium of uterus regenerates simultaneously during follicular phase of menstrual cycle.

D. The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of oestrogen which is essential for maintenance of endometrium.

Select the correct statement from the above?
questions.solution: The menstrual cycle is the reproductive cycle in all mammalian primate females. The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone which is essential for the maintenance of endometrium. The menstrual flow results due to the breakdown of the endometrium lining of the uterus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In human sperm, nebenkern refers to
questions.solution: Human sperm consists of head, neck, middle piece and tail. Head consists of nucleus and chromosomes and is covered by acrosome which contains enzymes to penetrate the ovum. The neck shows presence of proximal and distal centriole. Middle piece consists of mitochondria that are spirally arranged. These are known as Nebenkern. Tail consists of axial filament.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The non-cellular layer of the mature ovum is:
questions.solution: In females, the ovum is alecithal i.e. yolk is absent. The ovum membrane is the vitelline membrane. It is surrounded by zona pellucida. In between the vitelline membrane and zona pellucida there is a perivitelline space. Zona is a non cellular layer that prevents sticking of the ovum in the oviduct and thus prevents ectopic pregnancy. Surrounding this is the layer known as corona radiata that is secreted by granulosa cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Spermatogonia develop through:
questions.solution:
In testis, the immature male germ cells (spermatogonia) produce sperms by spermatogenesis that begins at puberty. The spermatogonia (sing. spermatogonium) present on the inside wall of seminiferous tubules multiply by mitotic division and increase in numbers. Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains 46 chromosomes. Some of the spermatogonia called primary spermatocytes periodically undergo meiosis. A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes, which have only 23 chromosomes each. The secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid
spermatids.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The uterus opens into ....A.... through a narrow ......B...... The cavity of the .......B....... is called .......C....... canal which along with .......A....... forms the .......D....... canal.
questions.solution: The uterus is single and it is also called womb. The shape of the uterus is like an inverted pear. It is supported by ligaments attached to the pelvic wall. The uterus opens into vagina through a narrow cervix. The cavity of the cervix is called cervical canal which alongwith vagina forms the birth canal.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: How many ova are released in the case of maternal twins and fraternal twins respectively in human?
questions.solution: Maternal twins are also called identical twins and are of same sex. They are genetically similar as they developed from single zygote or blastocyst.Fraternal twins are rare event in which one ovum are simultaneously released from each ovary. They are dissimilar or non-identical.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements about human reproduction:

II. The labia minora are fleshy folds of tissue, extend down the mons pubis, and surround the vaginal orifice.

III. Most of the major organ system of the fetus is formed by the end of the second month of pregnancy.

IV. The mammary glands of the female start producing milk during pregnancy.

How many statements are incorrect from the above?
questions.solution: A tertiary follicle is characterized by the presence of a fluid-filled cavity called the antrum. The labia majora are fleshy folds of tissue, extend down the mons pubis, and surround the vaginal orifice. Most of the major organ systems of the fetus are formed by the end of 12 weeks of pregnancy. The mammary glands of the female starts producing milk during pregnancy.

options: release ovum from the graffian follicle
make necessary changes in the endometrium for implantation
help in the development of corpus luteum
help in the collection of the ovum after ovulation
questions.solution: The part of the fallopian tube (oviduct) closer to the ovary is the funnel-shaped infundibulum. The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriate, which help in collection of the ovum after ovulation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The female external genitalia comprises of all the following, except:
questions.solution: The female external genitalia include mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen and clitoris. Mons pubis is a cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair. The labia majora are fleshy folds of tissue, which extend down from the mons pubis and surround the vaginal opening. The labia minora are paired folds of tissue under the labia major. The opening of the vagina is often covered partially by a membrane called hymen. The clitoris is a tiny finger-like structure which lies at the upper junction of the two labia minora above the urethral opening.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Haploid cells found within the seminiferous tubules of the testis are
questions.solution: In spermatogenesis, spermatogonia undergoes mitosis and forms two primary spermatocytes. Each primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis 1 to form two secondary spermatocytes that undergo meiosis 2 to form four spermatids. Mitosis and meiosis 2 are equational divisions and thus the ploidy level of the daughter cells will remain the same. Meiosis 1 is reductional division and thus ploidy level reduces to half. Spermatogonia which is diploid cells will form primary spermatocytes that are diploid too. These diploid cells will form haploid secondary spermatocytes which will form haploid spermatids.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A significant amount of progesterone is produced by the
questions.solution: Progesterone is mainly the female sex hormone responsible for maintaining the endometrium of the uterus alongwithestrogen.It is also responsible for secondary sexual characters in females like development of mammary glands. It is secreted by corpus luteum. Corpus luteum forms after ovulation. This secretes progesterone so that after ovulation if the sperm enters the fertilised egg can easily get implanted in the uterus. Once the implantation is completed it is very important to maintain the endometrium till parturition. Thus progesterone is secreted by placenta too.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The sudden increase in which of the following hormone is directly responsible for the release of ovum from the Graafian follicle?
questions.solution: Luteinising hormone is secreted by the anterior pituitary. It increases suddenly in the middle of the menstrual cycle. This is called LH surge. It stimulates the membrane granulosa cells of the Graafian follicle to release more liquor folliculi. This causes the pressure inside the follicle to increase causing it to rupture. The ovum in the secondary oocycte stage is released along with some follicular cells. This is called ovulation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: All the following statement is incorrect, except:
options: The longest phase of menstrual cycle is follicular phase while the shortest phase is ovulatory phase.
The ovary behaves as an endocrine gland during the luteal phase and is responsible for the thickening of the endometrium.
The formation of haploid second polar body occurs just before ovulation.
Permanent cessation of menses is an indication of pregnancy.
questions.solution: The longest phase of the menstrual cycle is a luteal phase (around 13 - 14 days) while the shortest phase is an ovulatory phase (around 1 day). The formation of the haploid second polar body occurs just after ovulation within the fallopian tube once the sperm touches the ovum. Permanent cessation of menses is menopause. In pregnancy, menses stops temporarily and is regained after delivery of the child. Blastulation occurs within 4-5 days after fertilization. Fertilization occurs within two days after ovulation. So blastulation occurs within 7 days from ovulation when the uterus is still in the luteal phase

By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed, for example, the limbs and external genital organs are well-developed. The first movements of the fetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month. B is 15-20 in number in a breast

questions.solution: The mammary glands are paired structures (breasts) that contain glandular tissue and variable amount of fat. The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15-20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. The cells of alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of alveoli. The alveoli open into mammary tubules. The tubules of each lobe join to form a mammary duct.

questions.solution: In males, seminal vesicles and bulbourethral or Cowper's glands are paired accessory glands. The prostate gland is a single, unpaired chestnut shape gland. Epididymis and Vas deferens are paired male accessory genital ducts.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match the columns:
 
  Column I   Column II
(a) Parturition (p) Attachment of blastocyst to endometrium
(b) Gestation (q) Release of egg from Graafian follicle.
(c) Ovulation (r) Delivery of baby from uterus
(d) Implantation (s) Duration between conception and birth
(e) Conception (t) Formation of zygote by fusion of egg and sperm
    (u) Stoppage of ovulation and menstruation
questions.solution:
Parturition is the process by which the completely formed baby is delivered out from the uterus, at the end of pregnancy. It involves vigorous contractions of uterus, which enables the expulsion of the foetus.

Gestation is the period between conception and birth of the child. It is also known as pregnancy. The human gestational period is 9 months.

Ovulation is the process by which the ovum i.e. egg is released out from the Graafian follicle. It usually occurs on the 14th day of the menstrual cycle.

Implantation is the process by which the blastocyst gets attached to the endometrium. It usually occurs 7 days after fertilization.

Conception is the process by which a zygote is formed by the fusion of egg and sperm i.e. fertilization.

questions.solution: The mammary glands of the female undergo differentiation during pregnancy and starts producing milk towards the end of pregnancy by the process called lactation. This helps the mother in feeding the newborn. The milk produced during the initial few days of lactation is called colostrum which contains several antibodies (IgA) absolutely essential to develop resistance for the new-born babies.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these is incorrect about oogenesis?
options: Menopause occurs around 50 years of age.
questions.solution:
The process of formation of a mature female gamete is called oogenesis which is markedly different from spermatogenesis. Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (oogonia) are formed within each fetal ovary; no more oogonia are formed and added after birth. These cells start division and enter into prophase-I of the meiotic division and get temporarily arrested at that stage, called primary oocytes. 
The primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle grows in size and completes its first meiotic division. It is an unequal division resulting in the formation of a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body.
In human beings, menstrual cycles ceases around 50 years of age; that is termed as menopause.

questions.solution: In human beings, after one month of pregnancy, the embryo’s heart is formed. The first sign of growing foetus may be noticed by listening to the heart sound carefully through the stethoscope. By the end of the second month of pregnancy, the foetus develops limbs and digits. By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed, for example, the limbs and external genital organs are welldeveloped. The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month. By the end of about 24 weeks (end of second trimester), the body is covered with fine hair, eye-lids separate, and eyelashes are formed. By the end of nine months of pregnancy, the foetus is fully developed and is ready for delivery.

It has more or less equal quantity of cytoplasm and DNA as in uncleaved zygote.

questions.solution: Cleavage divisions are mitotic division, in which the single-celled zygote is connected into a multicellular morula. But during cleavage division, there is no growth of resultant daughter cell/blastomeres. So, the DNA content will increase, but there is no increase or insignificant increase in the amount of protoplasm.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The acrosome of sperm is derived from:
questions.solution:
Acrosome is the inverted cap like structure which is present on the sperm head. It is derived from the Golgi apparatus. Acrosome contains digestive enzymes like hyaluronidase. When the sperm comes in contact with the zonapellucida of the ovum, the acrosome releases these enzymes. They help in digestion of the zonapellucida and enable the sperm to penetrate the ovum. This is known as acrosomal reaction.

Mitochondria are present in the middle piece of the sperm. They provide the energy required by the sperm for fertilizing the ovum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Among the following, the incorrect statement about the formation of female gamete in humans is:
options: A layer of granulosa cells surrounds primary oocytes forming primary follicles.
Ovum is released in the secondary oocyte stage from the secondary follicle.
The ploidy level of oogonia and primary oocyte is the same.
A fluid filled cavity called antrum develops which leads to the formation of tertiary follicle.
questions.solution:
The sequence of oogenesis (formation of ovum) is as follows:

Millions of oogonia are added in a female fetal ovary after birth. These oogonia (2n) undergo division and lead to the formation of primary oocytes (2n). A layer of granulosa cells surrounds these oocytes, which leads to the formation of primary follicles. More and more layer of granulosa cells and a new theca surround these primary follicles which leads to the formation of secondary follicles A fluid filled cavity called antrum develops which leads to the formation of tertiary follicle. An unequal division of the primary oocyte in the tertiary follicle leads to the formation of a haploid secondary oocyte i.e. ovum and a tiny first polar body. The largets follicle formed is Graafian follicle. The ovum is released from the Graafian follicle in the secondary oocyte stage

questions.solution: The reproductive cycle in the female primates (e.g. monkeys, apes and human beings) is called menstrual cycle. In non-primate mammals like cows, sheep, rats, deers, dogs, tiger, etc., such cyclical changes during reproduction are called oestrus cycle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the given statements about the human reproductive system.

A. The uterus is an inverted pear-shaped organ.
B. Each testis possesses 150 testicular tubules.
C. Mammary tubules open into the mammary ducts.

How many of the given statements are incorrect?
questions.solution:
Testicular lobules: There are about 250 compartments in each testis. Each lobule has 1 to 3 highly coiled structures called seminiferous tubules, in which spermatogenesis takes place.
Uterus: The uterus is single and it is also called womb. The shape of the uterus is like an inverted pear. It is supported by ligaments attached to the pelvic wall. The uterus opens into vagina through a narrow cervix. The wall of the uterus has three layers of tissue. The external thin membranous perimetrium, middle thick layer of smooth muscle, myometrium and inner glandular layer called endometrium that lines the uterine cavity.
Mammary tubules: The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15-20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. The cells of alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of alveoli. The alveoli open into mammary tubules. The tubules of each lobe join to form a mammary duct. Several mammary ducts join to form a wider mammary ampulla which is connected to lactiferous duct through which milk is sucked out.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following can result in breaking of hymen?
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution:
Hymen

- It is the membranous structure partially covering the vagina.

- It is usually torn during the first intercourse (coitus) but can also be torn or broken by a sudden fall/jolt / jerk/vaginal tampon insertion/active participation in sports like horse riding, cycling, etc.

- In some women, hymen may sometimes persist even after coitus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If Vasa efferentia gets blocked, the gametes will not be transported from:
questions.solution: Vasa efferentia are fine ciliated ductules that arise from the seminiferous tubules of the testis (where sperms are formed) and open into epididymis which is a mass of long narrow closely coiled tubule lying along the inner side of testis. Epididymis stores the sperms. Thus, if vasa efferentia gets blocked, sperms will not be transported from testis to the epididymis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following sets represents the external genitalia of a human female?
questions.solution: The female external genitalia include mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen and clitoris. Mons pubis is a cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair. The labia majora are fleshy folds of tissue, which extend down from the mons pubis and surround the vaginal opening. The labia minora are paired folds of tissue under the labia major. The opening of the vagina is often covered partially by a  membrane called hymen. The clitoris is a tiny finger-like structure which lies at the upper junction of the two labia minora above the urethral opening.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The function of Sertoli cells is controlled by:
questions.solution:
The function of Sertoli cells, also known as nurse cells is controlled by the Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH). The function of these cells is to provide nutrition to the growing germ cells i.e. spermatogonia. FSH stimulates the Sertoli cells to perform this function.

Estrogen is the hormone responsible for development of female sexual characters and development of female gametes.

Testosterone is the hormone responsible for development of male sexual characters and development of male gametes.

Luteinizing Hormone (LH) is the hormone responsible for induction of ovulation and maintenance of corpus luteum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these hormones targets sertoli cells for the production of androgen binding protein and favours spermiogenesis?
questions.solution: Spermatogenesis starts at the age of puberty due to a significant increase in the secretion of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH). This, if you recall, is a hypothalamic hormone. The increased levels of GnRH then acts at the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of two gonadotropins – luteinising hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). LH acts at the Leydig cells and stimulates synthesis and secretion of androgens. Androgens, in turn, stimulate the process of spermatogenesis. FSH acts on the Sertoli cells and stimulates the secretion of some factors like androgen binding proteins which help in the process of spermiogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
From the following statements about the menstrual cycle, which two are correct?
(i) Lack of menstruation may be indicative of pregnancy.
(ii) The changes in the ovary and the uterus are induced by changes in the levels of ovarian hormones only.
(iii) LH surge induces ovulation.
(iv) If fertilization occurs, the corpus luteum degenerates immediately.
questions.solution: Lack of menstruation in a normal female may be indicative of pregnancy. During pregnancy, the levels of estrogen and progesterone are high in the blood, which is required for the maintenance of uterus and thus, menstruation does not occur, On the 14<sup>th</sup> day of the menstrual cycle, there is a rapid increase in LH (called LH surge), that induces ovulation. The changes in the ovary and the uterus are induced by changes in the levels of ovarian hormones and pituitary hormones. If fertilisation occurs, corpus luteum degenerates by the 16<sup>th</sup> week of pregnancy.
